title: Censored-eclipse hunt: total and deep eclipsers hidden in ZTF's detection-only light curves (Gaia white-dwarf locus + bridge, G 18.5-20.8)
what_we_would_find: Detached post-common-envelope WD+dM and WD+brown-dwarf binaries and eclipsing double white dwarfs whose eclipses are deeper than ZTF's per-frame headroom (depth > ~1.5-3 mag, i.e. total or near-total eclipses of a WD-dominated system), plus deeply eclipsing CVs and, as by-catch, VY Scl-type low states. These are precisely the systems that produce NO in-eclipse data points in the ZTF DR light curve, so every published Gaia+ZTF search (BLS/outlier statistics on detections) is blind to them unless a partial-eclipse point happened to survive. Deficit arithmetic: Gaia EDR3 WD catalogue has ~359k P_WD>0.75 objects; ~140k lie at dec>-28, G 18.5-20.8 (d~300-1000 pc for M_G 11-13). With a close-binary (P<1 d) fraction of 3-5% and eclipse probability 8-15% at those periods, 300-1000 eclipsers are expected in that bin; WD-locus selection preferentially keeps the WD-dominated (deep-eclipse) systems. All catalogues combined hold ~150-250 eclipsing WD+MS systems, most at G<19 (Parsons 2015 ~71; van Roestel 2021 18 new; Kosakowski 2022 4; Brown 2023 43; Rebassa-Mansergas 2025 63/920). So the faint bin is under-populated by a factor >=5. Realistic yield after vetting: 30-80 new eclipsing WD binaries with periods, a handful of WD+BD, and 5-15 CVs/WDs with multi-month low states.
data_sources: ZTF DR24 HATS light curves + objects table on S3 (s3://ipac-irsa-ztf/ztf/enhanced/dr24/lc/hats; bulk, no per-position rate limit)
IRSA TAP ztf.ztf_current_meta_sci (per-quadrant obsjd, field/ccdid/qid, maglimit, seeing, corner coordinates) for the expected-visit and per-frame limit model
Gaia EDR3 white-dwarf catalogue (Gentile Fusillo+2021, 1,280,266 candidates / ~359k P_WD>0.75) and Gaia DR3 astrometry (PM for drift control, RUWE)
Legacy Surveys DR10 (neighbours/blends, forced unWISE W1 for donor/AGN checks)
ZTF forced-photometry service (ZFPS) for <=200 finalists only

Prior-art lists for exclusion and as recovery controls: van Roestel+2021 (arXiv:2105.14028), Kosakowski+2022, Brown+2023 (arXiv:2302.11392), Rebassa-Mansergas+2025 (arXiv:2505.15895), Burdge+2020 ultracompacts, arXiv:2608.19493, VSX
selection: Sky: dec > -28, |b| > 10 (ZTF footprint minus the worst crowding), ~200k targets = Gaia WD locus (P_WD>0.75) at G 18.5-20.8 plus ~50k bridge objects (M_G 6-11, BP-RP<0.6, parallax_over_error>3). Cadence/epochs: ZTF g+r, 2018-2026, require >=300 good frames (catflags=0) covering the position; typical 400-1500. Statistic: for each frame i covering the target (from quadrant corners), compute an EMPIRICAL detection probability p_i = P(detected | m_ref, maglimit_i, seeing_i) calibrated on the 200 nearest reference-catalogue sources within +/-0.2 mag in the same quadrant-epoch; flag 'impossible misses' (p_i > 0.98, no detection). Candidate = >=6 impossible misses AND miss fraction >=3x the field/mag-matched control. Then run a binary BLS (detected=1 / miss=0) over 0.04-2 d with a phased-miss coherence statistic; accept if misses cluster in phase at >4 sigma against shuffled epochs. Expected funnel: 200k -> ~2-4k with excess misses -> ~300 with phase-coherent misses -> ZFPS forced photometry on <=200 -> 30-80 confirmed. Mandatory control (lesson 10): the pipeline must recover, on its own configuration, the known total/deep eclipsers at G>19 in van Roestel 2021 / Kosakowski 2022 before any absence claim.
main_false_positive_channel: Instrumental miss geometry: sources near quadrant edges, in ghosts/masks or bad columns miss at fixed (field, ccdid, qid) combinations rather than at fixed orbital phase - test miss-vs-quadrant independence and require misses across >=2 fields/quadrants. Second: high-proper-motion WDs drifting out of the DR association radius (misses increase monotonically with time; Gaia PM x 8 yr > 1 arcsec kills the candidate). Third: blends/deblender failures (misses correlate with seeing, not phase; check per-epoch centroid, lesson 4). Fourth: genuine aperiodic faint states (VY Scl / CV low states, WD-locus CVs) which are findings but not eclipsers.
credit_channel: VSX: new eclipsing WD binaries filed as EA (WD+dM) with period and ZTF DR + ZFPS in-eclipse forced-flux evidence (VSX accepts ZTF-only light curves; a forced-photometry in-eclipse point plus the period is the confirmation). Low-state by-catch: VSX subtype revision / AAVSO alert. Community-confirm: Warwick/Sheffield/Barcelona WD-binary groups and amateur eclipse timers for G<19 targets; no telescope needed for the filing itself.
why_not_already_done: The groups who would do this - van Roestel/Burdge (Caltech), Rebassa-Mansergas/Parsons (Barcelona/Sheffield), Brown et al. - searched ZTF DR3-DR10 DETECTIONS with BLS and faint-outlier statistics; total eclipses that fall below the 5-sigma frame limit produce no rows and were found only when a partial-eclipse point survived (their own papers note in-eclipse fluxes 'at or below the ZTF detection threshold' for brown-dwarf companions). They know forced photometry fixes it, but ZFPS at 10^5 positions is impractical and Rubin will deliver forced photometry natively, so the rational group move is to wait for Rubin (DP1 is data-rights-only, and Rubin's public stream is dark). A missing-epoch statistic joined to the exposure-metadata table is unglamorous engineering, not a paper topic, and DR24 doubles the baseline of the searches they published. What changed vs the dead Gaia-DR3 compact-object lanes: this is not astrometric/RV dark-companion hunting; the signal is a periodic absence in a censored photometric archive, a lever this session proved on ZTF19abxfaon.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 1 (ZTF DR light curves are censored; gaps relative to expected visits encode faint states), lesson 4 (per-frame limitmag is the honest reference; slope/centroid tests), lesson 7 (HATS/S3 bulk access sidesteps the ~1,100-query IRSA limit), lesson 2 (reference-catalogue seeding: only reference-catalogue objects have light curves, which is fine here because Gaia WDs at G<20.8 are in the reference), lesson 10 (recover known deep eclipsers on own config first).
feasibility_notes: All inputs are public/anonymous. Compute: ~200k light curves x ~1000 epochs = 2e8 rows plus ~20-30M metadata rows filtered by field - hours on the NUC. Software gate: HATS reading needs lsdb/hats or pyarrow+s3fs; the ostinato venv has a no-pip-install rule, so check what is present or ask the user to approve a throwaway venv. ZFPS is bound to the TU Delft email, batches <=1,500, results as browser downloads - keep finalists <=200. Archive-only confirmation is possible (forced in-eclipse flux + period); no accounts, no telescope. Rubin is not a competitor until at least DR1 (2027+, data-rights only). Estimated labour: 2-3 weeks including the recovery control; the same code is reused by lane 3 and can be re-run on nsc_dr2.meas in the DES-SN deep fields for r=21-24 (ZTF- and Gaia-blind) halo/thick-disc WD eclipsers (~3-10 expected in 27 deg^2).
novelty_per_labor_guess: HIGH: tens of new-to-knowledge eclipsing WD binaries (some WD+BD, possibly WD+WD) from ~2-3 weeks of work, plus low-state by-catch; failure mode is a null if the empirical detection-probability model is too noisy at G>20.3, which the control test exposes early.

title: Halo dwarf novae frozen in the DES-SN 2013-2018 seasons: hostless blue outbursts at r_peak 19-23 with no quiescent counterpart to r~26
what_we_would_find: Field halo / thick-disc cataclysmic variables at 5-50 kpc caught in dwarf-nova (mostly WZ Sge / period-bouncer-type) outburst: r_peak 19-23, blue (g-r<0.3) throughout, 1-4 week duration, no counterpart in the DES deep coadds (r~26.5 in C3/X3/E2; r~25.5 elsewhere), hostless. This class is essentially empty: outburst-identified CVs are catalogued to r_peak<~19.5 (CRTS/ASAS-SN/ZTF era) and the bulge DN of OGLE sit at 8 kpc in the plane, not the halo. Expected numbers: Galactic stellar halo ~1e9 stars x (CV per star in the disc = 4.8e-6 pc^-3 / ~0.1 stars pc^-3 ~ 5e-5) ~ 5e4 halo CVs; the 27 deg^2 DES-SN cone out to 50 kpc holds ~25; with recurrence 5-30 yr and 5 seasons x ~5 months of coverage, 3-12 halo outbursts are expected, plus 5-20 thick-disc SU UMa outbursts at 2-5 kpc (r_peak 16.5-19.5) in the E1/E2 fields (dec -43), which no northern survey covered at that depth in 2013-2018. Even 2-3 confirmed objects would be new-to-knowledge members of a nearly empty class (halo CV space density is unmeasured).
data_sources: NSC DR2 via Astro Data Lab TAP (anonymous): nsc_dr2.meas (dated per-exposure detections), nsc_dr2.object, nsc_dr2.exposure, nsc_dr2.chip (chip footprints for coverage proof); NSC DR2 spans 2012-Oct 2019 so all five DES-SN seasons are included
DES DR2 coadd catalogue and the DES Deep Fields catalogue (Hartley+2022; r~26.5 in SN-C3, SN-X3, SN-E2, COSMOS) for quiescent-counterpart limits
Legacy Surveys DR10 (host galaxies to r~24.5, forced unWISE W1/W2 for AGN rejection)
DES-SN published lists for exclusion/identification: Pursiainen+2018 rapidly evolving transients (72), Wiseman+2020 host coadds, DES-SN5YR photometric SN catalogue
CRTS, ASAS-SN, ATLAS, ZTF (2018+) for recurrence and for the bright-end control; VSX/SIMBAD/TNS per-object prior-art check
selection: Sky: the 10 DES-SN fields (C1-C3 at dec -28, X1-X3 at -5, E1-E2 at -43, S1-S2 at 0; 27 deg^2 total, deep fields C3/X3). Epochs: MJD 56500-58200, r (and g,i,z where available); ~150-250 shallow-field epochs per band over five ~5-month seasons at 5-7 d cadence, ~800 r exposures/deg^2 in the deep fields (per lesson 6); single-epoch depth r~23.5 (shallow) / ~24.5 (deep). Candidate: cluster of >=3 nsc_dr2.meas detections on >=2 distinct nights within a 40-d window (rule 10: never single-night chains), position covered by >=100 r exposures (chip-footprint join, lesson 9), r_peak 16.5-23, g-r<0.4 at peak, no DES deep-coadd source within 1 arcsec brighter than r_peak+5 (or none to the limit), no LS DR10 galaxy within 3 arcsec to r 24.5, per-epoch centroid scatter <0.3 arcsec and no linear motion (rejects slow movers, lesson 4), duration above threshold 5-35 d, decline >0.1 mag/d after plateau. Funnel: ~5,000 SN-like candidates -> hostless & <=35 d -> 100-300 -> shape/colour (DN: rise <=3 d, plateau 5-20 d, stays blue; SNe redden and last 40-90 d) -> 10-40 finalists -> manual. Control: recover known CRTS/ASAS-SN dwarf novae inside S1/S2/X fields and Pursiainen's hostless RETs on the same pipeline before any absence claim.
main_false_positive_channel: Hostless or faint-host supernovae (SLSN and Ia/Ibc in dwarf hosts below r 25) - separated by duration and post-peak reddening; second: slow solar-system movers at r 20-23 lingering 2-4 weeks in a field (centroid drift test); third: AGN flares in coadd-undetected hosts (WISE colour, extendedness); fourth: template/ghost artefacts and M-dwarf flares (single-epoch, red quiescent counterpart); fifth: Galactic microlensing/novae (longer, achromatic or red).
credit_channel: VSX (UG/UGWZ type with the DECam outburst light curve; DECam photometry is acceptable evidence). For a >10 kpc halo CV, a short co-authored note per the user's publication policy, with CV-population groups (Pala/Inight/Schreiber) as consumers of halo space density; TNS is not appropriate for 2013-2018 events. Rubin DDF teams (ECDFS/EDFS/ELAIS-S1/XMM-LSS overlap the DES-SN fields) are natural follow-up consumers for the next outburst.
why_not_already_done: DES-SN (Kessler pipeline; Wiseman, Pursiainen, Sullivan) built their selection around host association, SN-like durations and photometric classification; hostless 2-3 week events with no host were scored as junk or 'Galactic' and never catalogued. Pursiainen+2018 required SN-like fits and mostly hosted events. The CV community (Szkody/ZTF, Kato/vsnet, Rodriguez/eROSITA) operates at r<20 in the ZTF/ASAS-SN/X-ray regimes and has no DECam deep-field pipeline. The NSC meas table is unglamorous, and the Rubin DDF teams will own this regime from 2026 data onward - but the 2013-2018 DES epochs are frozen and cannot be scooped from Rubin data; the objects can only be rediscovered at their next outburst 10-30 years later. Distinct from the dead 'turn-on' lane: here both the transient and its non-detection are measured in the SAME instrument/pixel scale (DECam vs DECam deep coadd), so the blend/sub-threshold/cosmic-ray failure mode of comparing a deep sharp survey against a shallow coarse one does not apply.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 6 (nsc_dr2.meas dated per-exposure rows; DES-SN deep fields ~800 r exposures/deg^2), lesson 4 (per-epoch centroids kill movers and blends), lesson 8 (LS DR10 forced unWISE for AGN rejection), lesson 9 (prove coverage with chip footprints before any non-detection claim), lesson 10 (recover known DES-field dwarf novae first), rule 10 from the precovery campaign (>=2 nights, never single-detection chains).
feasibility_notes: All public, anonymous Data Lab TAP (use async jobs per field; meas rows selected by exposure list to stay under row limits). Deep-field catalogues are downloadable. Compute is small (10^7-10^8 meas rows). Archive-only confirmation is partial: the outburst light curve, colour, hostlessness and deep-coadd non-detection are all archival; a spectrum is impossible (object is at r>26 now), so the claim is 'halo dwarf nova candidate' with a quantified SN-rejection - acceptable for VSX as UG:. Estimated labour 2-4 weeks. Main risk: period-bouncer recurrence times >30 yr could make the halo outburst rate 3x lower than estimated, giving a null; the thick-disc E-field sample (r_peak 16.5-19.5) is the insurance yield.
novelty_per_labor_guess: MEDIUM-HIGH: few objects (3-15) but each is a member of an almost empty class (field halo CV identified by outburst beyond 5 kpc), the epochs are un-scoopable, and the pipeline is reusable for any deep multi-epoch DECam field in NSC.

title: The missing nova-likes: blue non-periodic flickerers at 1-4 kpc and |b|>15 in ZTF DR24 (G 17-20.5), with an 8-year low-state (VY Scl) census
what_we_would_find: New nova-like (UX UMa / VY Scl / SW Sex-type) cataclysmic variables - high-accretion-rate CVs that never outburst - at G 17-20.5, i.e. 1-4 kpc and 0.3-2 kpc above the plane, including high-|z| nova-likes (a population whose very existence in the thick disc is untested) and systems caught in multi-month VY Scl low states. Deficit arithmetic: the local nova-like density is (2-5)e-7 pc^-3 (3-5 NLs within ~150-200 pc: IX Vel, V3885 Sgr, TT Ari, ...; Pala+2020 CV density 4.8e-6 pc^-3 with ~10% NL fraction); with a 260-300 pc scale height, integrating the dec>-28, |b|>15 cone to G=20 (Mv +4.5+/-1) predicts roughly 1,500-3,000 nova-likes, whereas VSX holds only ~400 NL/UX/VY-type objects in total, of which perhaps 200 at |b|>15 - a >=5x deficit concentrated at G>17, where Gaia parallaxes are >30% uncertain, eRASS1 depth (~5e-14 cgs) only reaches Lx~1e31 to ~1.3 kpc, and no Halpha survey exists outside the J-PLUS/S-PLUS footprints. Yield: 30-80 new nova-like candidates plus 5-15 objects with low states, and a measured VY Scl duty-cycle distribution across the whole high-latitude NL population (Duffy+2024, arXiv:2411.07744, did 8 systems).
data_sources: Gaia DR3 (G, BP-RP, parallax, PM, RUWE, classprob_dsc_combmod_quasar) and Culpan+2022 hot-subluminous candidate catalogue (~61.6k) as the main contaminant/parent sample
ZTF DR24 HATS objects table (rms, chi2, ngood per band) for the flicker-excess screen, then HATS light curves for survivors; ztf_current_meta_sci for the low-state gap census
GALEX (GUVcat / Gaia-GALEX crossmatch) FUV-NUV; Legacy Surveys DR10 grz + forced unWISE W1-W2 (AGN rejection)
J-PLUS DR3 (~3,000 deg^2 north) and S-PLUS DR4 (~3,000 deg^2 south): J0660-r Halpha excess where covered - coverage must be proven per object (lesson 9)
VHS / UKIDSS J,K for donor detection (K 15-17 at 1-3 kpc gives a period/distance constraint)

Prior-art exclusion: VSX, Inight+2023 SDSS CV catalogue (arXiv:2304.06749), Abrahams+2022 Gaia CV candidates, Rimoldini+2023 Gaia DR3 'CV' class (7,306), Rodriguez+2025 eROSITA volume-limited samples, Szkody ZTF CV papers, DESI CV catalogue (arXiv:2607.22836)
selection: Sky: dec > -28, |b| > 15 (~15,000 deg^2). Parent: Gaia G 17-20.5, dereddened BP-RP < 0.5, and either parallax_over_error>5 with M_G 3-8 (the bridge / hot-subdwarf region) or parallax_over_error<5 with PM S/N > 5 (at G 19 sigma_PM ~0.4 mas/yr, so PM>2 mas/yr; kills QSOs), classprob_quasar<0.3, LS DR10 W1-W2<0.5 or W1 undetected. Expected parent ~40-60k. Variability screen from the HATS objects table (no light-curve download): >=150 good epochs in g and r; rms_g >= 3x the field- and magnitude-matched median rms AND >= 0.08 mag; excess present in both g and r. Then light curves for ~1-3k survivors: reject periodic sources (Lomb-Scargle / BLS peak with FAP<1e-3 whose folded amplitude explains >50% of the variance; removes sdB reflection/ellipsoidal binaries, RR Lyrae, delta Sct), require a slope of mag-vs-frame-limitmag ~0 (real source, lesson 4) and per-epoch centroid scatter consistent with an isolated point source; ~300-600 remain; add GALEX FUV-NUV<0.5 or NUV excess and J0660 excess where covered. Low-state census on all survivors AND all known VSX nova-likes in the footprint: impossible-miss runs of >=30 d (lesson 1 statistic from lane 1) = candidate VY Scl state. Manual vetting of ~100 -> 30-80 filed candidates. Control: the pipeline must recover known VSX nova-likes at G 17-20 in the footprint at >=80% before any density claim.
main_false_positive_channel: Residual quasars with spuriously significant Gaia PM (RUWE>1.4, close neighbours) and blended pairs whose seeing-dependent photometry mimics flickering - both killed by per-epoch centroid tests, LS DR10 neighbour lists and W1-W2; second: unresolved periodic variables (sdB reflection systems, delta Sct, RR Lyr) - periodogram cut; third: quiescent dwarf novae and polars (also CVs, so still a discovery but a different subtype); fourth: ZTF quadrant-level calibration scatter (compare with field-matched controls).
credit_channel: VSX: file as CV: with subtype note (NL: / VY:) using ZTF light curve, colours, UV and (where available) Halpha excess; VSX moderators may withhold the NL subtype pending spectroscopy, so the filing is a new CV with evidence, not a spectral type. Low-state detections: AAVSO alert / AstroNote and VSX subtype revision. Consumers: SDSS-V MWM CV programme (Gaensicke/Inight) and eROSITA CV groups accept candidate lists for spectra; amateur spectroscopists (ARAS) can confirm Balmer emission for G<17.5 targets.
why_not_already_done: Nova-likes fall through every dominant CV discovery channel: they do not outburst (invisible to the alert-driven channels that Kato/vsnet, ZTF/Fink/ALeRCE and Szkody's ZTF spectroscopy run on), they are X-ray faint at >1 kpc (Rodriguez+2025's eROSITA+Gaia volume-limited samples are complete only to 150-300 pc), and the Gaia-based CV searches (Abrahams+2022; Rimoldini+2023's 7,306 Gaia 'CV' candidates; the 2025 unsupervised MS-WD-valley study, arXiv:2510.23776) rely on Gaia's ~40-70 epochs, which cannot see 0.1-mag flickering at G>18. The hot-subdwarf community (Culpan/Geier/Schaffenroth) mines the same Gaia region but searches ZTF for PERIODIC variables and treats non-periodic scatter as noise. SDSS-V will slowly spectroscopize the bridge, but its carton is Gaia-CMD-driven with parallax cuts that exclude 2-4 kpc objects. What changed: ZTF DR24 (8 yr, 300-1,500 epochs at G 18-20.5), bulk HATS access, and the censoring lever that turns a 60-day gap into a low-state detection.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 7 (HATS objects table gives rms/chi2 for 10^5 sources without per-position queries), lesson 1 (detection gaps = low states; VY Scl census for free), lesson 4 (limitmag-slope and centroid tests separate flickering from threshold noise and blends), lesson 8 (LS DR10 forced unWISE W1-W2 for QSO rejection), lesson 9 (prove J-PLUS/S-PLUS/GALEX coverage before citing a null), lesson 5 (VHS/UKIDSS J,K donor detection), lesson 10 (recover known nova-likes on own config first).
feasibility_notes: All archives are public/anonymous; the heavy step is one pass over the HATS objects table (no light-curve download for the parent) - hours on the NUC; light curves only for ~1-3k survivors. Same HATS software gate as lane 1 (lsdb/hats or pyarrow+s3fs in a venv the user approves). Archive-only confirmation is partial: flickering + blue + UV + PM + (Halpha) supports 'CV' strongly enough for VSX, but the NL subtype needs a spectrum (community-confirm mode). Labour ~2 weeks after lane 1's tooling exists. Risk: the local NL density is based on 3-5 objects, so the predicted deficit carries a factor-3 uncertainty; the pipeline's recovery rate on known VSX nova-likes is the gate that decides whether to continue past the first 1,000 deg^2.
novelty_per_labor_guess: MEDIUM-HIGH: many new-to-knowledge CVs for low labour, plus a phenomenon-level result (VY Scl low-state duty cycles across the whole high-latitude population); per-object novelty is 'new CV' rather than a new class, and VSX subtype acceptance is the main friction.

title: SPHEREx-native 'new mid-IR source since NEOWISE died' sweep of the southern Galactic plane (obscured novae, eruptive YSOs, dusty mergers)
what_we_would_find: Dust-obscured Galactic classical novae (A_V ~ 5-25) and other eruptive IR transients (FUor/EXor outbursts, ILRT/merger-type dusty transients) that erupted AFTER NEOWISE stopped observing (Aug 2024) and that no optical survey could see. Each survivor is a never-reported nova/eruption, i.e. a new-to-knowledge object with its own designation. The Galactic nova rate is 47.9 (+3.1/-8.3) per yr (De+2023, NEOWISE) while optical surveys report ~10-15/yr; >50% of the missed events sit at A_V >~ 5 in the inner southern plane. NEOWISE recovered ~22 previously-missed novae in 10 yr at a comparable 6-month cadence, so the honest expectation for the 16 months of QR2 data (May 2025 - Sep 2026) is ~3-6 missed novae plus ~10-30 eruptive YSOs/dusty transients, most of them south of dec -20 where no IR time-domain survey is currently operating (WINTER/PGIR are Palomar-north; VVVX ended 2023; Gattini ended). The SPHEREx spectrum itself (Br-alpha 4.05 um, Br-beta 2.63 um, Pfund series, CO 4.6-5.0 um at R~110-130) gives a first-look classification.
data_sources: SPHEREx QR2 spectral-image MEFs (bands 4-6, 2.42-5.0 um, plus band 3 for colour), anonymous S3 bucket s3://nasa-irsa-spherex (no account) and IRSA SIA2 collection 'spherex_qr2' with ~1-day ingestion lag; weekly cadence

unWISE full-depth NEO7 coadds and CatWISE2020 (W1/W2 to ~2020) as the static mid-IR reference; NEOWISE single-exposure photometry 2014-Aug 2024 as the 'was it already bright' test; LS DR10 forced unWISE fluxes (W1 > 19.3 Vega limits) where DECaLS covers
VVV / VVVX (K to ~18, 2010-2023), UKIDSS GPS, 2MASS as the near-IR static reference and for blend checks at 0.34" resolution
Gaia DR3 proper motions (propagate every source within 15" to epoch 2025.5 before declaring 'no counterpart')
ZTF DR24/25 light curves and ATLAS forced photometry (where accessible) to confirm optical absence; MPC/MPChecker for minor-planet rejection; TNS cone search for prior reports
selection: Region: Galactic plane |b| <= 5 deg, l = 280 deg through 0 deg to +30 deg, dec < -20 deg prioritized (~1,100 deg^2; the full plane is ~3,600 deg^2 as a stretch). Per-channel single-pass 5-sigma depth is ~17.1-18.1 AB at 3.8-5.0 um and ~18.8-19.1 AB at 0.75-3.8 um (the published 17.8-18.8 / 19.5-19.9 AB figures are the 4-pass cumulative depth), i.e. W2-equivalent ~14.2 Vega and W1-equivalent ~16.2 Vega per pass before confusion. Candidate = source detected at >= 5 sigma in >= 3 distinct channels within bands 4-6, from exposures taken at different times (minutes to days apart) and at different detector positions, with W1-eq <= 15.0 Vega and W2-eq <= 13.5 Vega; AND no unWISE NEO7 / CatWISE counterpart within 6" brighter than W1 = 17 (unWISE full depth is >= 3 mag deeper than our threshold, so absence is real); AND no NEOWISE single-exposure detection 2014-2024 within 6"; AND no 2MASS/VVV K <= 14 counterpart at the PM-propagated position. Epochs: SPHEREx pass 1 (May-Dec 2025) and pass 2 (Dec 2025-May 2026) plus the current weekly pass-3 images; run as a weekly sweep on the freshest images (filing-latency lesson). Expected raw candidates before vetting: ~10^3 per 1,000 deg^2 per pass, dominated by persistence ghosts and blends; expected survivors: ~2-5 novae + ~10-30 eruptive YSO/dusty transients over the whole QR2 span.
main_false_positive_channel: (1) H2RG persistence/latent images of bright stars from the previous 11.8-arcmin small-step pointing: a ghost lands at a sky position with no counterpart. Killed by requiring >= 3 channel detections from exposures at different detector positions (a latent stays fixed in detector coordinates, a real source stays fixed on the sky). (2) Unresolved blends of two faint red stars at the 6.2" pixel that look 'new' against unWISE (also 6") but resolve in VVV/UKIDSS at 0.34"-0.9". (3) Main-belt asteroids/comets where the plane crosses the ecliptic (l ~ 0-10 deg in Sgr, l ~ 190 deg): killed by requiring position consistency < 3" across exposures separated by >= 6 h and an MPChecker query. (4) SAA / particle-hit flagged exposures (use the per-pixel status flags; ~1.5% of exposures flagged). (5) LPVs caught at 2MASS/WISE minimum: excluded automatically because any LPV bright enough for our threshold is in NEOWISE. Mandatory control (lesson 10): recover the three classical novae and two FUors classified in Karambelkar, De et al. 2026 ApJL as blind detections on the pipeline's own configuration before any absence claim.
credit_channel: TNS AT report (Galactic novae and IR transients are accepted; discovery credit = first filer) + TNS AstroNote with the SPHEREx spectrum; VSX entry for the nova once classified; community confirmation by IR spectroscopy from the De/Karambelkar/Sokoloski group or Munari/Woodward nova people (co-authorship channel consistent with the publication policy). 'First SPHEREx-discovered nova' is an honest object-specific claim.
why_not_already_done: The group that would do this is Karambelkar, De, Hillenbrand, Sokoloski (Columbia/Flatiron/Caltech). Their 2026 ApJL explicitly used NEOWISE 2014-2024 ZOGY differencing as the discovery engine and SPHEREx only to classify already-detected transients; SPHEREx-native discovery is their obvious next step but (a) the LVF design (wavelength varies per pixel) and the 3-6" PSF make classical difference imaging awkward, so nobody has built a SPHEREx subtraction pipeline yet; (b) their stated future is WINTER/PGIR/PRIME/Cryoscope integration, all northern or not yet flying; (c) they publish on a months-to-year cadence and do not file TNS reports for Galactic-plane events. The SPHEREx project itself has no transient pipeline (the 'transient flagging' paper arXiv:2607.02809 is about particle hits on the detectors) and no point-source catalog yet. The southern inner plane after Aug 2024 is therefore an unwatched IR window. Risk: De's group could stand up SPHEREx differencing at any time; the window is probably 6-12 months. What changed relative to the dead 'IR novae' lane: that lane mined NEOWISE/VVV-era archives that De's group had already exhausted; this lane uses a NEW epoch (2025-26) that did not exist when they published, on a mission with no real-time transient product.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 3 (a source that turned on and stayed bright generates no alerts): SPHEREx has no broker at all, so a catalog-level 'present now, absent in the static reference' test is the only detector. Lesson 8 (unWISE coadds give deep contemporaneous W1 limits for free) supplies the reference. Lesson 5 (near-IR archives barely used) supplies VVV/UKIDSS blend control. Lesson 9 (prove coverage before citing a null): VVV/VVVX/unWISE-NEO7 footprints and SPHEREx per-position channel completeness must be queried, not assumed. Lesson 10 (recover own template on own configuration) is the mandatory nova control. Filing-latency lesson: sweep the newest weekly images, file the same day.
feasibility_notes: Access: S3 anonymous (aws s3 --no-sign-request) satisfies 'no new accounts'; SIA2 via pyvo for footprint lookups. Volume: each 116.9-s exposure yields six 3.5x3.5 deg images each spanning 17 channels, so covering area A in all channels of one detector needs ~17 x (A/12.25 deg^2) images; for 1,100 deg^2 and three detectors that is ~4,600 MEFs (~40 MB each) ~ 180 GB per pass, streamed and discarded, forced-photometry compute trivial on enzo. Do not use per-position IRSA cutouts for the blind step (lesson 7: IRSA rate-limits at ~1,100 queries with silent empty 200s). Archive-only confirmation is real: the SPHEREx spectrum (Br-alpha/Br-beta/CO) distinguishes nova from YSO from LPV, and the NEOWISE/VVV absence establishes eruption timing; spectroscopic classification still needs a professional IR spectrum. VERIFIED RELEASE-STATUS LEDGER (checked 2026-09-19): SPHEREx QR2 weekly since Oct 2025, two all-sky passes done (Dec 2025, ~May 2026), no point-source catalog; eROSITA-DE DR2 released 31 Jul 2026 (catalog-only, eRASS:3 stacked; consortium sat on eRASS:5 internally for 4 yr, so no solo edge); Rubin early DP2 released 27 Jul 2026 but RSP access is data-rights-only with a 'narrow request-based' path for unaffiliated researchers, and the public alert stream is dark since MJD 61235, so Rubin is excluded; Euclid DR1 12 Nov 2026 (consortium has had it internally; UCD and transient work packages exist); DESI DR2 spectra not until early 2027; LoTSS DR3 Feb 2026 (Callingham/Vedantham radio-stars group at ASTRON/Leiden owns that cross-match); SDSS DR20 Sep 2026 (Gansicke/Inight CV sweeps and the BHM consortium own it); VLASS epoch-4 half-epoch ongoing (Caltech Hallinan/Dong/Somalwar own epoch differencing); Einstein Probe WXT alerts are team-internal. None of these offers a solo edge comparable to the three lanes here.
novelty_per_labor_guess: MEDIUM-HIGH: few objects (single digits of novae plus tens of eruptive YSOs over the QR2 span) but each is a named, TNS-creditable, headline-grade discovery in a window nobody is watching; infrastructure cost is front-loaded (~2-3 weeks) and is the same plane forced-photometry engine that Lane 2 needs, then reusable weekly.

title: First all-sky Paschen-alpha / Brackett-alpha point-source census: obscured emission-line stars (symbiotics, Be/B[e], Wolf-Rayet, PNe) behind A_V 8-25 in the Galactic plane
what_we_would_find: Emission-line stars that H-alpha surveys structurally cannot reach. Pa-alpha (1.875 um) lies inside the telluric water band and has never been surveyed from the ground; IPHAS/VPHAS+ H-alpha reach only A_V <~ 6-8. SPHEREx now gives Pa-alpha, Pa-beta (1.282), Br-gamma (2.166), Br-alpha (4.052, R~130), He I 1.083 and He II 1.012/1.163/1.693 for every K <~ 15 star on the sky, twice. Target classes and the size of the missing population: symbiotic stars (~300 confirmed vs 3x10^3-4x10^5 predicted; the dusty D-types and the obscured bulge/plane ones are almost entirely unfound); Galactic Wolf-Rayet stars (~700 known vs 1,900 +/- 250 predicted, the missing ~1,000 at A_K 1-3 and K 10-14, with He/H line EWs of 100-2,000 A that are trivial at R~41); obscured classical Be and B[e] stars (order 10^4 exist at K < 14 in the plane; a few thousand are catalogued); obscured PNe central stars, LBV candidates, nova remnants and Herbig Ae/Be stars. Realistic new-to-knowledge yield after vetting: several hundred to a few thousand emission-line objects, including tens of WR and symbiotic candidates.
data_sources: SPHEREx QR2 spectral-image MEFs, all six detectors, both completed passes (pass 1 May-Dec 2025, pass 2 Dec 2025-May 2026), from s3://nasa-irsa-spherex (anonymous) with IRSA SIA2 footprint queries
Target list: VVV/VVVX + UKIDSS GPS + 2MASS point sources with K <= 14.0 Vega and isolation (no neighbour within 12" brighter than K+1)
Gaia DR3 (astrometry, XP colours, RUWE) and 2MASS J-K for temperature/extinction priors; unWISE W1-W2 for dust excess

Templates/controls: BeSS Be-star catalogue, Rosslowe & Crowther Galactic WR catalogue (~700), NODSV symbiotic database (~300 confirmed), HASH PNe, IPHAS (Witham+2008, 4,853 H-alpha emitters) and VPHAS+ emitters for cross-validation at low A_V
Gaia DR4 epoch photometry (2 Dec 2026) and ZTF/ATLAS/NEOWISE light curves to supply the variability evidence that VSX requires
selection: Sky: |b| <= 3 deg over l = 10-350 deg (exclude the innermost bulge |l| < 10 deg for confusion), ~2,000 deg^2; ~10^7 isolated K <= 14 targets after the isolation cut (~10-20% of the 5x10^7 plane sources at K < 14). Photometry: forced PSF photometry at every target in every channel using the exposure-averaged PSF in the MEF, per pass separately. Line index per line: E = (F_line - F_cont)/F_cont with the continuum interpolated from the two channels on each side; channel width at Pa-alpha is lambda/R ~ 457 A, so E >= 0.15 corresponds to EW >= ~70 A; at Br-alpha (R~130, ~310 A wide) E >= 0.15 is EW >= ~47 A. Detection: |E| >= 0.15 at >= 5 sigma with continuum SNR >= 20 per channel (single-pass per-channel 5-sigma ~19 AB at 1.9 um means SNR 20 at ~17.5 AB ~ K 16 Vega in uncrowded sky; the K <= 14 cut keeps us well above the confusion floor), required in BOTH passes and in >= 2 of the lines (Pa-alpha + Br-alpha, or Pa-alpha + Pa-beta, or He I 1.083 + Br-gamma). Tiers: Tier A (WR/symbiotic/PN-like: E >= 0.5 in >= 3 lines, expected ~100-500 objects); Tier B (Be-like: E 0.15-0.5 in Pa-alpha and Br-alpha, expected ~2,000-5,000, of which perhaps half uncatalogued). Expected control recovery: >= 80% of BeSS Be stars with K < 12 and known Pa-alpha emission, >= 95% of catalogued WR stars with K < 13 in the footprint.
main_false_positive_channel: (1) Temporal variability masquerading as spectral features: a single-pass spectrum is assembled from exposures spread over ~2 weeks (and the two passes are 6 months apart), so Miras, YSOs and eclipsing systems produce channel-to-channel jumps. Killed by requiring the excess to be confined to the line channels with smooth continuum on both sides, present in both passes, and by rejecting known LPVs (Gaia DR3 LPV table, NEOWISE variability). (2) The 1.8-2.0 um H2O absorption trough of M giants/supergiants, which makes the 1.875 um channel look like a peak relative to its neighbours: killed with a J-K/Gaia colour prior and by demanding Pa-beta or Br-alpha confirmation, which are in clean windows. (3) CO bandhead absorption at 2.29-2.4 um distorting the Br-gamma continuum. (4) Crowding: aperture contamination at 6.2" pixels is the reason for the isolation cut and the |l| > 10 deg exclusion. (5) LVF wavelength-calibration errors near detector edges (use the per-pixel wavelength WCS and drop edge rows). Mandatory template controls (lesson 10): blind recovery of BeSS, WR and NODSV objects on the pipeline's own configuration before any claim of a new emitter.
credit_channel: VSX for every object with demonstrable photometric variability (types BE/GCAS for Be stars, ZAND for symbiotics, WR; Gaia DR4 epoch photometry from 2 Dec 2026 will supply variability evidence for essentially all of them), named credit per object; a catalogue paper (A&A/RNAAS) with professional co-authors for the WR/symbiotic candidates, which need confirming spectra: Crowther/Rosslowe (WR), Merc/Munari/Akras (symbiotics), Drew/Mohr-Smith (OB/Be). Community-confirm mode fits exactly: we find, they take the spectrum, credit stays by name.
why_not_already_done: The SPHEREx Galactic working group's published outputs are diffuse maps (Murgia+2026 Br-alpha/PAH mapping, the ices investigation) and ultracool-dwarf spectra (SUDA); a point-source emission-line census is not a team deliverable and the project has not yet released a point-source catalog (planned within three years), so anyone doing this now must build forced photometry on hundreds of GB of LVF images in crowded fields. The emission-line-star specialists (Drew's IPHAS/VPHAS+ group at Hertfordshire, Crowther's WR group at Sheffield, Merc's symbiotic group, the BeSS community) are optical/spectroscopic and small, and Crowther's group just spent its effort on Gaia XP WR candidates (A&A 2025). The extragalactic Pa-alpha work (arXiv:2608.08393) targets galaxies. Nobody has had two SPHEREx passes over the plane for more than ~4 months. Honest risk: an IPAC/Caltech SPHEREx-team member could do the plane in a summer; the window is likely 6-18 months until the first team point-source catalog makes it trivial.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 5 (near-IR archives barely used): VVV/UKIDSS give the target list, blend control and the extinction ladder. Lesson 7 (IRSA per-position rate limit): forces the bulk-S3 image-level design instead of 10^7 cutout requests. Lesson 9 (prove coverage): SPHEREx per-position channel completeness must be queried per pass because SAA-flagged and re-observed exposures leave channel gaps in the plane. Lesson 10 (template recovery on own configuration). Lesson 12 / Gaia DR4 timing: DR4 epoch photometry arrives 2 Dec 2026 and converts spectroscopic finds into VSX-filable variables at scale.
feasibility_notes: Same plane forced-photometry engine as Lane 1, extended to all six detectors: ~17 x (2,000/12.25) x 6 ~ 17,000 MEFs per pass (~0.7 TB per pass, streamed and discarded), two passes; compute is trivial (10^7 positions x 102 channels of PSF-fit photometry). Anonymous S3, no accounts. Archive-only confirmation is partial: the SPHEREx spectra themselves classify WR (He II/He I/Br-gamma widths at R~41 are still diagnostic), PNe (Pa-alpha dominating) and D-type symbiotics (dust continuum + lines) with reasonable confidence; classical Be vs Herbig vs YSO needs a ground spectrum, hence the community-confirm design. Pipeline validation gates: (i) recover the Karambelkar+2026 novae and known BeSS Pa-alpha emitters as blind detections; (ii) run the IPHAS/VPHAS+ emitter lists at A_V < 6 as an external truth set and report completeness vs K and A_K; (iii) shape-check outputs (harness rule).
novelty_per_labor_guess: HIGH: the physics guarantees a large missing population, the measurement is genuinely new (no ground survey can do Pa-alpha), the yield is hundreds-to-thousands of uncatalogued objects per unit labor once the engine exists, and it shares its infrastructure with Lane 1. The cost is that VSX credit is per-object only after variability is shown, and the exotic tiers (WR, symbiotics) need professional spectra.

title: Gaia DR4 day-1 single-eclipse / single-dip search via TAP-only vari_summary statistics, aimed at the 2014-2020 southern faint window no other survey covered
what_we_would_find: Stars that showed one deep, unrepeated dimming event in Gaia's 66-month epoch photometry (25 Jul 2014 - 20 Jan 2020): long-period eclipsing binaries with a single observed eclipse (epsilon Aur / EE Cep / J1407-type disk eclipsers, wide WD/BD/dark-companion eclipses), 'big dipper' dust/disk occultations, and rare giant-blink events (VVV-WIT-08 class). The unique window is G 14-19 at dec < -30 deg (no ZTF; ATLAS south only from 2022; ASAS-SN V to ~17 only) plus all-sky G > 17 before 2018: events only Gaia recorded and that will never repeat on any other survey's watch. Gaia DR3 released epoch photometry for only 10.5 M pre-selected variables and 'hardly any' long-period EBs were found because of the scanning law; DR4 provides epoch photometry for all 2.8 G sources and a 403 M-row vari_summary with per-source statistics, and there is no single-dip module among the DR4 variability tables (eclipsing_binary 2.39 M is period-based; microlensing 1,360; short_timescale 8.4 M; LPV 4.4 M).
data_sources: Gaia DR4 (2 Dec 2026): gaiadr4.vari_summary (403,061,676 rows; min/max/median/skewness/kurtosis-type statistics per band, as in DR3), vari_classifier_result (315 M), vari_eclipsing_binary (2.39 M), then DataLink epoch_photometry (FOV-transit level) for the survivors only; epoch_astrometry for centroid/blend checks on finalists
Gaia DR3 vari_summary + epoch_photometry (10.5 M sources) for pipeline development and template recovery before 2 Dec
ASAS-SN big-dipper sample (JoHantgen, Rowan, Kochanek et al. 2025: 31 objects at 13 < g < 14; 13 single-eclipse EBs, 7 multi-eclipse, 11 dippers) and TYC 2505-672-1 as recovery controls

ZTF DR24/25, ATLAS, ASAS-SN Sky Patrol, NSC DR2 per-exposure measurements (nsc_dr2.meas, lesson 6) and VVV for post-2018 or southern repeat checks; Gaia Observation Forecast Tool (GOST) for predicted-vs-actual transit counts
SIMBAD/VSX/Gaia DR3 classification tables to remove catalogued periodic variables
selection: Stage 1 (TAP only, no bulk download, week 1-2 after 2 Dec 2026): from vari_summary select num_selected_g_fov >= 30, (median_mag_g_fov - min_mag_g_fov) >= 0.4 mag, (max_mag_g_fov - median_mag_g_fov) <= 0.10 mag, skewness_mag_g_fov >= +1.5, and the dip depth >= 8x the robust scatter; join gaia_source for G, parallax, RUWE, dec; prioritize dec < -30 deg and G = 14-19 (unique window), keep the bright north as the ASAS-SN control. Expected Stage-1 survivors: ~10^5-3x10^5. Stage 2: DataLink epoch_photometry in 5,000-ID chunks; require >= 2 FOV transits inside the dip (the two Gaia fields of view give paired transits ~106 min apart and scans 6 h apart, so a real multi-day dip reproduces on the same night: the rule-10 analogue), all dip transits unflagged, and BP/RP epoch fluxes dropping consistently (achromatic or reddened, not one band only). Stage 3: remove sources with a period in vari_eclipsing_binary/vari_classifier_result, catalogued variables, and star-forming-region YSO dippers unless exceptional; then external light curves for any repeat and NSC/VVV per-exposure for southern targets. Expected counts: ASAS-SN found 19 new single/long-period dip objects among 5.1 M stars over ~7 yr (rate ~5x10^-7 per star-year); scaled to 403 M vari_summary sources over 5.5 yr with a ~25-40% chance that Gaia's ~70-100 transits catch a multi-day dip twice, ~300-500 detectable single-dip systems all-sky, of which ~100-200 lie in the unique southern/faint window and are new-to-knowledge.
main_false_positive_channel: Gaia epoch-photometry systematics: single-transit outliers from crowded scans, satellite/bright-star proximity, transits near CCD gaps and scan-angle-dependent blending, which produce isolated low points in tens of millions of sources. Killed by the paired-transit rule (>= 2 FOV transits in the dip), per-transit rejection flags, BP/RP consistency and epoch_astrometry centroid stability. Second channel: genuine but uninteresting classes sampled once (short-period EBs whose other eclipses fell between scans, RCB declines, LPV minima): mitigated with the classifier tables, colours and external light curves; note that an uncatalogued RCB decline or short-period EB in the southern faint window is still a VSX-filable new variable. Third channel (lesson 1, censoring): a dip deeper than ~2.7 mag on a G ~ 18 star drops the source below Gaia's G ~ 20.7 onboard detection limit and appears as MISSING transits, not faint ones; compare actual transit epochs against GOST-predicted visits to recover these.
credit_channel: VSX new-variable submissions with Gaia DR4 epoch photometry as the light-curve evidence (VSX accepts Gaia G data; types EA with period unknown, DIP for dust/disk dippers), named credit per object; an AstroNote for any class-level result (e.g. a disk-eclipser candidate with a Gaia-only eclipse) and a co-authored paper if a professional group takes up follow-up. Filing within the first 2-4 weeks is the whole game.
why_not_already_done: It cannot be done before 2 Dec 2026. DPAC CU7 (Eyer, Rimoldini, Holl) classify periodic classes and will publish DR4 variability papers; a one-off dip is not a class their supervised pipeline emits, and there is no dip table in the DR4 contents list. The groups that would do it afterwards are Kochanek/Rowan/JoHantgen (ASAS-SN big dippers; they will extend to the bright end where ASAS-SN already covers), Tzanidakis/Davenport (ZTF dippers), and the Cambridge alerts group; El-Badry-type groups will spend the first months on astrometric binaries and NSS, not dips. Their constraint is priority, not capability: the amateur's edge is a pipeline validated on DR3 in advance, a TAP-only pre-filter that avoids the 7.2 TB epoch_photometry download, and willingness to hand-vet a few hundred candidates and file to VSX within weeks. Honest risk: the window is about 1-3 months, and Gaia archive congestion in week 1 may push execution to week 2-3.
session_lesson_exploited: Rule 10 / lesson 10 reincarnated as the paired-FOV-transit requirement (a dip must reproduce on the same night in both fields of view; never accept a single transit). Lesson 1 (censored light curves encode faint states): missing transits versus GOST-predicted visits reveal dips below Gaia's detection floor. Lesson 6 (NSC per-exposure measurements and DES deep-field cadence) and lesson 5 (VVV) give southern repeat checks. Lesson 9: prove that ZTF/ATLAS/ASAS-SN actually covered the epoch and depth before claiming an event is Gaia-only. Filing-latency lesson: prepare drafts and the VSX form logic before 2 Dec.
feasibility_notes: Preparation Oct-Nov 2026 on DR3: same vari_summary column set exists in DR3, so the Stage-1 query and Stage-2 logic are testable now on 10.5 M sources, with recovery of TYC 2505-672-1 (already proven as a control in the DASCH lane), EE Cep-type objects and any ASAS-SN big dippers that have DR3 epoch photometry. Execution needs only Gaia archive TAP (async, partition by source_id/HEALPix ranges since a 403 M-row scan may time out) and DataLink (5,000 IDs per request); no bulk download, no new accounts, compute trivial. Archive-only confirmation is possible for the Gaia-only window in the sense that the event is real and unrepeated; physical classification (disk eclipse vs dust vs companion) needs colour behaviour and follow-up, which is the community-confirm step. Expect heavy archive load in the first week after 2 Dec 2026; the lane is time-boxed to roughly Dec 2026 - Feb 2027.
novelty_per_labor_guess: HIGH but time-boxed: tens to ~200 genuinely new, unrepeatable single-dip variables in a window nobody else recorded, obtainable with a TAP-only pipeline that can be built and validated before the release; value decays within months as professional groups reach the same table, so the labor must be spent before 2 Dec and in the first three weeks after.

title: Visit-deficit census: ZTF sources whose low state has no rows (expected-visit vs detection count, quadrant-exact)
what_we_would_find: Uncatalogued deep-low-state systems whose faint state lies below the ZTF single-epoch limit and therefore never appears in the light curve: polars and VY Scl nova-likes with high state 16<r<18.5 and drops >=2.5 mag (low state r>=20.5-21.5), R CrB / dust-obscuration declines lasting months-years, Gaia17bpp-like giant obscurations, and eclipsing systems with >=2.5-mag eclipses (WD+dM, disk-eclipsing binaries). The observable is a contiguous run of >=10 deep frames (limitmag > target+2) spanning >=3 nights in which a magnitude-matched control star <3' away is detected and the target is not. Population arithmetic: Pala+2020 CV density 4.8e-6 pc^-3 scaled to d<700 pc gives ~4,000 CVs in the northern high-latitude sky, ~800 polars + ~100 nova-likes, of which ~30% have high state <=18.5 and drops >=2.5 mag => order 300 fully-censored state-cyclers, 60-70% of them absent from PolarCat (>200 polars, arXiv:2505.10337) and Ritter-Kolb/VSX; plus tens of dust events and deep eclipsers. Realistic post-vetting yield: 10-50 new-to-knowledge objects, each filed to VSX with the ZTF gap + control + (where present) a DECam/LS DR10/PS1 detection of the faint state, and classified where an archival LAMOST/SDSS-V/DESI spectrum exists (He II 4686 => magnetic).
data_sources: IRSA TAP ztf_objects_dr24 (columns oid, field, ccdid, qid, fid, ngoodobs, nobs, medianmag, refmag, magrms, minmag, maxmag) or the same object-level columns via column-projected reads of s3://ipac-irsa-ztf/ztf/enhanced/dr24/lc/hats (anonymous)

IRSA TAP ztf.ztf_current_meta_sci (per-frame polygon ra1..dec4, obsjd, maglimit, seeing, expid) and ztf.ztf_current_meta_ref (reference startobsdate/endobsdate, nframes, maglimit) for the exact expected-visit count per source
ZTF DR24 HATS nested light curves (hmjd, mag, catflags) fetched by object-ID index for the deficit tail only; IRSA LC API (limitmag, expid per epoch) for the final few hundred
Gaia DR3 HATS (data.lsdb.io) for neighbour/blend kill (any Gaia source within 4" brighter than target) and proper motion
Legacy Surveys DR10 (grz + forced unWISE W1/W2) and PS1 DR2 for an independent faint-state or IR-excess measurement; LAMOST DR10/11, SDSS DR19, DESI DR1 spectra for classification without a telescope
selection: Sky: full ZTF footprint dec > -28, |b| > 5 (~22,000 deg^2), r band primary, g band as independent confirmation. Sources: 16.0 < medianmag_r < 18.5, ngoodobs >= 100, |refmag - medianmag| < 0.5 (kills the 1-2-detection asteroid/cosmic-ray-on-reference-noise population that dominated the naive tail in the pilot), reference epoch known from meta_ref. Expected visits per source = number of DR24-epoch science frames (obsjd <= DR24 cutoff, ~2025-10-20 in the pilot quadrant; using the 'current' metadata table without this cut manufactures a spurious 12% deficit for every source) whose polygon contains the PM-propagated position and whose maglimit > medianmag + 1.0. In the pilot quadrant this reference is a delta function (median 1044, p90 1046 of 1183 frames), so flag deficit >= 30 frames (>=3%). Catalogue-level kills before any light curve is read: distance to nearest quadrant edge >= 5' (97% of the naive interior tail was pointing-jitter loss within 5'); no Gaia DR3 source brighter than the target within 4" (the one deblend case in the pilot: a G=16.8 P=1.13 d EB 2.5" away); no second deficit source within 2' (the 5-object cluster in the pilot); Gaia PM < 150 mas/yr. Pilot rates: 0.36% of well-behaved interior bright sources survive to this stage (~360k sky-wide from ~100M sources), ~50% removed by the neighbour and cluster kills => ~150-200k light-curve reads. Light-curve stage: longest contiguous run of missed deep frames vs a control within 3' of the same magnitude; require >=10 frames spanning >=3 distinct nights with >=2 nights separation (pilot survivors all failed this: single high-cadence nights, <=9 frames); require the g-band gap to coincide. Depth floor is limitmag(frames) - medianmag >= 2.0. Mandatory positive control before the sky pass (lesson 10): recover known ZTF-era low states, e.g. the VY Scl sample of arXiv:2411.07744 (MV Lyr's ~200 d low that fell in a visibility gap) and 5-10 PolarCat polars with 2019-2024 lows, on the pipeline's own configuration.
main_false_positive_channel: Geometric and blend censoring that mimics a fade: (1) quadrant-edge pointing jitter, measured to extend 4-5' inward (63% of visits at 3.0', 89% at 4.0'); (2) seeing-dependent deblending next to a brighter neighbour, which yields detections only in the best-seeing season (the pilot's strongest catalogue candidate: 64 of 73 detections in 2019); (3) local systematics near bright stars/galaxies producing clusters of deficit sources; (4) high-cadence partnership nights where a source is missed on tens of frames within one night (small, non-contiguous over nights); (5) high-proper-motion stars leaving the match radius; (6) large-amplitude periodic red variables (Miras with r_min below the limit) - killed by periodicity of the detected segments and W1 brightness; (7) known objects - killed by the existing known-object front filter + VSX/SIMBAD.
credit_channel: VSX (new variable, types AM/NL/VY/RCB:/E with a light curve showing the gap and the control star; named discoverer), following the one filing already completed; AstroNote for any object caught in an ongoing low state that pros can spectroscopically classify; archival spectra (LAMOST/SDSS-V/DESI) supply classification without a telescope.
why_not_already_done: The Caltech ZTF variability group (van Roestel, Guidry, Caiazzo, Kupfer) ran exactly this dropout idea in September 2026 (arXiv:2609.08923) but through NEGATIVE ALERTS and only on 273k Gaia white dwarfs, visually inspecting 4,027 objects; extending negative alerts to 10^8 field stars is junk-dominated (bright-star halos, galaxies, saturated wings) and their interest is WD debris, not CVs or dust events. Dip searches (Tzanidakis 2025, arXiv:2508.03964; ASAS-SN big dippers, arXiv:2507.19594) require points INSIDE the dip, so a sub-limit fade is invisible to them by construction; the VY Scl ZTF paper (arXiv:2411.07744) explicitly could not measure the depth of lows that fell in gaps. The ZTF DR objects table 'ngoodobs' was never framed as a completeness statistic and anyone who tries it naively sees a tail that is 97% quadrant-edge jitter and 1-2-detection junk (I measured both) and abandons it; the per-frame polygons and limits in ztf_current_meta_sci that make it exact are in a separate metadata table nobody joins to the objects table. CV specialists (Szkody, Inight, Kato/vsnet, Schwope's PolarCat) work from known-object lists. Rubin DIA forced photometry will report non-detections natively from ~2028, so the window is the next 18 months. Not a recycle of the closed bimodal state-cycler search: that lane required BOTH states detected in ZTF (bimodal magnitude histogram); this lane targets systems whose low state produces no rows at all, which the bimodal statistic cannot see.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 1 directly (ZTF DR light curves are censored: no rows below the limit) turned into the primary selection statistic; lesson 4 (per-frame limitmag as the honest detection reference) for the depth floor; lesson 7 (HATS/S3 bulk endpoint, IRSA per-position limit ~1,100) dictates the two-stage catalogue-then-index-lookup design; lesson 9 (prove coverage) implemented as per-frame polygon containment; lesson 10 (template recovery on the pipeline's own configuration) as the mandatory positive control; lesson 5/8 (VHS/LS DR10 forced WISE) for faint-state and dust classification.
feasibility_notes: Tested today on one quadrant end-to-end (objects table pull 35 s; 5,769 sources; light curves for 5 survivors + 1 control via the LC API; Gaia/SIMBAD/VSX checks). Sky pass: object-level columns for ~1.5B r-band objects via column-projected parquet reads of the DR24 HATS (~50-100 GB) or ~1,800 per-field TAP queries (~35 s each, ~18 h); meta_sci per field (1,800 queries, rows ~75k each). Compute: numpy point-in-polygon for ~3,000 sources x ~1,000 frames per quadrant x ~115k quadrants is hours on the 6-core NUC. Light-curve stage ~150-200k targeted reads through the HATS object-ID index (days, not weeks); do not use the per-position LC API for this stage (rate limit manufactures nulls, lesson 7). Confirmation is archive-only: gap + control + limitmag depth + optional DECam/LS/PS1 faint-state detection + archival spectrum; no new accounts needed (IRSA TAP, S3 anonymous, Gaia TAP, VSX API all open). Gaia DR4 (2 Dec 2026) epoch photometry will independently date any fade that began 2014-2017.
novelty_per_labor_guess: High: ~2-3 weeks of pipeline + vetting for an expected 10-50 new-to-knowledge deep-low-state systems (mostly uncatalogued magnetic/nova-like CVs, a few dust events), a class transient surveys and within-detection variability pipelines are structurally blind to; pilot quadrant null (0/3,000) is consistent with the ~1e-5 per-source rate, so the census must run sky-wide to pay off.

title: DECam-epoch state snapshot: NSC DR2 per-exposure measurements >=2 mag off the ZTF bright state (both directions, detections only)
what_we_would_find: Systems caught by DECam (2012-09 to 2019-11) in a state that ZTF (2018-2026) has never seen: (a) ZTF-bright stable sources (17.5<r<19.5) that a dated DECam exposure recorded 2-5 mag fainter => a low state that ended before or straddled the ZTF era (VY Scl, polars, deep eclipses, dust dips); (b) DECam-bright point sources (17<r<19.5 on >=2 nights) whose ZTF object is >=2 mag fainter and flat => faded 2013-2018 and stayed down (long-low-state polars/NLs, R CrB or Gaia17bpp-like obscurations still ongoing, 2013-2019 Galactic novae/CV outbursts never reported). Expected counts: ~10-15M ZTF sources with >=2 DECam r epochs in -30<dec<+30; using the same population arithmetic as lane 1 restricted to the DECaLS/DES overlap (~10,000 deg^2, |b|>18) gives ~150-300 undiscovered polars/NLs in the magnitude window, of which ~30-60% are caught in a low state with 3 random DECam epochs at 10-30% low-state duty cycle => ~50-150 direction-(a) candidates of which ~half uncatalogued; direction (b) yields fewer (<=10-20) but includes the unreported-transient class filable to TNS with a 2013-2019 discovery date.
data_sources: NOIRLab Data Lab TAP (anonymous sync works; verified today): nsc_dr2.object, nsc_dr2.meas (dated per-exposure mags, exposure id, flags), nsc_dr2.exposure (mjd, filter, exptime, depth), nsc_dr2.chip (per-CCD footprint) - 25,304 DECam r exposures with exptime>=60 s at -30<dec<+30, MJD 56193-58803
ZTF DR24 objects table / HATS (medianmag, magrms, refmag, ngoodobs) and nested light curves for the ZTF-epoch state at the DECam dates where they overlap (2018-07 to 2019-11)
Gaia DR3 for PM propagation to the DECam epoch and for the neighbour/blend flux-sum test
Legacy Surveys DR10 catalogue (its own DECam epochs 2014-2019, plus forced unWISE W1/W2 for dust vs accretion classification) and PS1 DR2 (2010-2014 epochs) as a third state sample
DES-SN deep fields C/S/X inside ZTF (~8 deg^2, ~800 r exposures/deg^2 at weekly cadence 2013-2018) as a high-cadence sub-lane where a whole low state can be sampled
selection: Region: ZTF x DECam overlap -30 < dec < +30 with >=2 NSC r-band exposures deeper than 22.0 on >=2 nights (DECaLS 3-pass band ~9,000 deg^2 at |b|>~18; DES wide dec>-30 ~1,500 deg^2; DECaPS strips where they cross ZTF). Direction (a): ZTF objects 17.5 < medianmag_r < 19.5 (DECam saturation r<~16.5-17 in 90 s frames excluded with margin), magrms < 0.10, ngoodobs >= 100, |refmag-medianmag| < 0.3, PM-propagated to each DECam exposure MJD; require an NSC meas row within 1.0" in r (or g with a colour term) with mag_DECam - median_ZTF >= 2.0, on >=1 exposure, with the SUM of all NSC fluxes within 3" of the ZTF position also >=2.0 mag fainter (kills ZTF blends), meas flags clean, position >20 px from chip edge (nsc_dr2.chip), and a second DECam exposure on a different night either also faint (extended low) or at the ZTF level (bounded event). Direction (b): NSC objects with nphot_r >= 2 on >=2 nights, class_star-like morphology, 17 < rmag < 19.5, rms < 0.15, matched to ZTF: object absent or medianmag_r >= rmag_DECam + 2 with magrms < 0.2 and refmag consistent (i.e. faint since the 2018 reference), Gaia G consistent with the DECam bright state (Gaia epoch 2014-2017) or Gaia absent; prove ZTF coverage via meta_ref/meta_sci polygons. Explicitly EXCLUDED: any 'no DECam detection' or 'no ZTF object at r>20' logic - that is the closed turn-on lane and its blend/noise failure modes; here both epochs are secure detections and the comparison is flux vs flux. Pilot first on one DECaLS-covered ZTF field at dec~+10 with the same template-recovery rule (known VY Scl/polar with a documented 2013-2019 low, e.g. from arXiv:2411.07744 or PolarCat, must reproduce on the pipeline before any absence claim).
main_false_positive_channel: Direction (a): DECam saturation/bleed and non-linearity of bright stars (r<17), scattered-light and pupil ghosts, CCD-edge/bad-column partial flux, and ZTF blends whose components DECam resolves (defeated by the 3" flux-sum test rather than the nearest-match); asteroids matched to a faint NSC object are irrelevant here because the requirement is a faint DETECTION of a known bright source. Direction (b): cosmic rays/satellite glints at r~18 in a single DECam exposure (killed by the >=2-night rule), asteroids (same), and Gaia-epoch transients that are real but already in Gaia Alerts/TNS/VSX (front filter). Both: proper motion not propagated, and NSC DR2 photometric zero-point outliers on individual exposures (check with the same-exposure neighbour residuals, which NSC exposes via meas rows of every neighbour).
credit_channel: VSX for Galactic variables (NL/VY, AM, RCB:, E with deep eclipse) with the DECam faint-state epoch quoted; TNS discovery report with the historical DECam discovery date for any unreported 2013-2019 transient (TNS accepts past discovery dates); AstroNote if a currently-low object needs prompt spectroscopy.
why_not_already_done: NSC's own variability metrics (variable10sig, rms) are within-NSC MAD statistics that a 1-3 exposure excursion barely moves (lesson 6), and the NSC team (Nidever) built the catalogue for astrometry/photometry, not for cross-survey state comparison; the Legacy Surveys team does not do variability at all; DES variability work is confined to the SN fields; the ZTF team compares to Gaia and PS1, not to DECam epochs. Cross-survey 'faded star' searches exist only at the century scale (VASCO: USNO-B vs PS1) or within one survey. The obstacle is purely labour: joining 68 billion dated NSC measurements to ZTF requires per-exposure footprint handling and a flux-sum blend test, and nobody's science case needed it because the CV community (Szkody, Inight+2023 Gaia CVs, SDSS-V, Schwope) starts from spectroscopic or X-ray selection. NSC DR3 does not exist as of today (checked datalab.noirlab.edu and the literature), so DR2's 2012-2019 window is the fixed archive - which is the kind of asset (fixed archive, no stream) the community scan identified as best for a solo worker.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 6 (nsc_dr2.meas has dated per-exposure measurements; the object-level flags are MAD statistics) is the core lever; lesson 1 (DECam caught ZTF19abxfaon in a state ZTF could not see) is the proof of principle; the turn-on lane's structural lesson (deep-sharp vs shallow-coarse is satisfied by blends/noise) is inverted into a detection-vs-detection flux comparison with a 3" flux-sum blend test; lesson 8 (LS DR10 forced unWISE W1 limits) separates dust events from accretion lows; lesson 9 (coverage proof via chip footprints and ZTF frame polygons).
feasibility_notes: Anonymous Data Lab TAP sync queries work (verified today: exposure-table aggregates returned in <1 min); bulk extraction by 1-deg^2 boxes over ~10,000 deg^2 is ~10k queries at ~30 s (3-4 days wall-clock, run on the NUC in the background); meas rows are pulled only for the ~10^4-10^5 mismatch candidates. ZTF side from the DR24 HATS/objects table as in lane 1. No new accounts. Compute trivial. Confirmation is archive-only (two dated detections in two states; LS DR10 third epoch; archival spectra for classification). Risk: NSC DR2 astrometric-epoch handling for PM stars must be tested with a known high-PM control before any mismatch is believed.
novelty_per_labor_guess: Medium-high: ~2 weeks for an expected 20-70 uncatalogued state-changers plus a small chance of unreported 2013-2019 transients; lower per-object ambiguity than lane 1 because both states are measured fluxes, but smaller sky area and only 2-4 DECam epochs per source.

title: Turn-off census: Gaia DR3 sources (2014-2017) that are >=2 mag fainter or absent in the ZTF reference era (2018-2026) - the total-censoring limit, staged for Gaia DR4 epoch photometry
what_we_would_find: Objects that faded by >=2 mag between the Gaia DR3 photometric epoch (2014.5-2017.4) and the ZTF reference build (2018-2019) and have stayed faint for up to 8 years, so they are entirely absent from ZTF variability products and from every broker (lesson 3 in reverse): R CrB stars in decade-scale declines (R CrB itself took 2007-2018), polars/VY Scl in multi-year lows, Gaia17bpp-class giant obscurations, YSO/disk-eclipse events, dust-enshrouded post-merger remnants, and Gaia-epoch transients (2014-2017 novae/outbursts that entered DR3 as mean-bright sources but were never reported). Expected counts: ~100M Gaia sources with G<18.5, dec>-28, |b|>10; genuine multi-year >=2-mag faders are ~10^-6 to 10^-5 of field stars => order 100-1,000 sky-wide, most of them catalogued if bright (<15) but largely uncatalogued at G=16-18.5; realistic post-vetting yield 5-30 new-to-knowledge long-duration faders and 0-5 unreported Gaia-epoch transients. This is the complement of lane 1: lane 1 finds gaps inside ZTF light curves; this finds sources ZTF never had a bright state for.
data_sources: Gaia DR3 gaia_source (HATS at data.lsdb.io or ESA TAP): G, BP-RP, phot_g_n_obs, phot_g_mean_flux_over_error, astrometric_params_solved, ruwe, PM; Rybizki+2022 fidelity for spurious-source rejection; Gaia DR3 variability tables and Gaia Science Alerts archive for the known-transient filter

ZTF DR24 objects table / HATS (refmag, medianmag, ngoodobs per filter) and ztf.ztf_current_meta_ref (reference epoch and polygon) + meta_sci (frame polygons) to PROVE the position was covered by a built reference
IRSA ZTF reference-image cutouts (via ztf_current_path_ref) for pixel-level checks of the strongest ~100 candidates

PS1 DR2 (2010-2014), NSC DR2 (2012-2019) and LS DR10 (2014-2019, with forced unWISE W1/W2) to bracket the fade date and separate dust (IR-bright) from accretion (IR-faint) fades; VHS/UKIDSS/2MASS J,K for the same
Gaia DR4 (2 Dec 2026) epoch photometry to date each fade within the Gaia window once released
selection: Gaia DR3: G < 18.5, dec > -28, |b| > 10, astrometric_params_solved = 31, phot_g_n_obs >= 30, fidelity > 0.5, no Gaia neighbour within 3" brighter than G+1 (ZTF PSF-fit merging), not within the ZTF bright-star mask radius of any G<8 star. Predict ZTF r from G and BP-RP using the published Gaia-to-ZTF colour transformations (validated on the 99% of sources that match normally). Crossmatch at the PM-propagated 2019.0 position with 1.5" (primary) and 3" (secondary) radii to the ZTF r and g objects tables. Candidate if EITHER (i) no ZTF object within 3" while meta_ref shows a reference built at that position and meta_sci shows >= 50 DR24-epoch frames with maglimit > r_pred + 2 containing it, OR (ii) the matched ZTF object has refmag >= r_pred + 2 AND medianmag >= r_pred + 2 with magrms < 0.3 and ngoodobs >= 20 (faint since the reference; the flat faint light curve is the confirmation that this is not a within-ZTF variable). Require the g band to agree. Then bracket the epoch: PS1 (2010-14) bright?, NSC/LS DR10 dated DECam epochs bright or faint?, W1 excess? Strongest candidates get reference-image cutout inspection (bright-star spikes, ghosts, chip gaps). Expected funnel: ~0.1% of 100M fail the primary match (~100k), dominated by crowding and masks; coverage proof and the 3" flux logic reduce to ~10^4; the flat-faint-light-curve branch (ii) is cleaner and is where most real objects will sit. Positive controls before any absence claim: R CrB-type stars with documented 2016-2018 declines, and any PolarCat/VSX object known to have been low throughout 2018-2020, must be recovered by the pipeline on its own configuration.
main_false_positive_channel: Crowding/astrometric mismatch (ZTF PSF-fit catalogue merging a Gaia pair into one object at a shifted centroid), bright-star masks and saturation ghosts in the ZTF reference, chip gaps in the primary field grid not covered by the secondary grid at that position, Gaia spurious sources near bright stars (fidelity cut), colour-transformation outliers for extreme colours (very red M/C stars, blue WDs - use BP-RP-dependent tolerance, require >=2 mag), and Gaia-epoch transients that are already in Gaia Alerts/TNS/VSX (front filter). Blends are NOT a channel in this direction: Gaia resolves finer than ZTF, so blending can only make the ZTF source brighter than predicted, never fainter.
credit_channel: VSX for Galactic long-duration faders (RCB:, NL/VY, AM, or UNIQUE with the multi-survey bracketing shown); TNS for an unreported 2014-2017 transient with the historical discovery date; AstroNote if an object is still faint and a pro spectrum during the low state would classify it. After DR4, a Gaia-epoch light curve of each object becomes citable directly.
why_not_already_done: The Gaia DPAC variability group (Eyer, Rimoldini) crossmatches Gaia to literature variables, not to ZTF completeness; the ZTF/Gaia forward comparisons (e.g. Gaia DR3 variable WDs vetted by ZTF, A&A 2026) ask whether Gaia-flagged variables vary in ZTF, never whether Gaia-mean-bright sources are missing from ZTF. VASCO (Villarroel) works at the USNO-to-PS1 century scale with plate-artefact-dominated lists; nobody has run the Gaia(2015)-to-ZTF(2019+) version because it looks like a bookkeeping crossmatch whose raw tail is 99% crowding and masks, and a proof-of-coverage step against per-frame polygons is required to make an absence claim (lesson 9) - a step catalogue-level crossmatchers skip. The Caltech negative-alert WD search (arXiv:2609.08923) cannot see this class at all: a source already faint when the reference was built generates no alerts, positive or negative (lesson 3). Gaia DR4 in December 2026 will give every source an epoch light curve, which will make this a one-week job for DPAC or anyone - so the solo advantage is to have the ZTF-side coverage-proven candidate list ready before DR4 lands. What changed relative to the closed turn-on lane: that lane compared NSC r=22-24 noise-limited detections against ZTF and drowned in blends, sub-threshold noise and cosmic rays; this lane's reference state is a G<18.5 five-parameter astrometric Gaia source with >=30 transits (not noise, not a cosmic ray) and the comparison direction (sharp-bright -> coarse-faint) is the one blending cannot fake.
session_lesson_exploited: Lessons 2 and 3 (ZTF light curves are seeded from the reference; a source in the wrong state when the reference was built is invisible to per-position lookup and to every broker) define the target class; lesson 9 (prove coverage before citing a null) is operationalised via meta_ref/meta_sci polygons; lesson 7 (bulk HATS instead of per-position API) makes the 10^8-row crossmatch feasible; lesson 8 (LS DR10 forced unWISE) and lesson 5 (VHS/UKIDSS) classify dust vs accretion fades; lesson 12 (check DR4/DESI/Rubin status) - DR4 is the second stage of this lane, not a prerequisite.
feasibility_notes: LSDB crossmatch of Gaia DR3 (G<18.5, |b|>10, dec>-28: ~1e8 rows) against the ZTF DR24 objects HATS on the 6-core NUC: partition-wise, ~1-2 days, all anonymous S3/HTTPS; ESA Gaia TAP for spot checks (verified today). meta_ref/meta_sci per field via IRSA TAP (~1,800 queries). Reference cutouts via IRSA IBE for ~100 objects only. No new accounts. Expect the first pass to be dominated by nuisance (crowding, masks); budget most of the labour for the coverage-proof and flux-sum logic, and pilot on 100 deg^2 at b~+30 and 100 deg^2 at b~+12 before scaling. Positive-control recovery is mandatory; if no known 2016-2018 fader is recovered, the pipeline is broken, not the sky.
novelty_per_labor_guess: Medium: ~2-3 weeks for an expected 5-30 uncatalogued long-duration faders (and a small chance of an unreported Gaia-epoch nova); lower yield than lane 1 but the objects are individually rarer and the same pipeline becomes a DR4 day-one lane on 2 Dec 2026, when the Gaia-side epoch photometry will date every fade for free.

title: Sub-Gaia parallax census of the DES supernova deep fields (5-parameter refits of nsc_dr2.meas)
what_we_would_find: New nearby objects fainter than Gaia (r or z = 21-24, G>20.7) with 5-sigma trigonometric parallaxes measured from ~300-1,400 dated DECam exposures per band: cool and ultracool white dwarfs (T_eff<5,000 K, including CIA/IR-faint ones) at 80-200 pc, mid/late-L and early-T dwarfs at 35-100 pc (z-band astrometry), and ultracool halo subdwarfs at 200-400 pc. Expected ~5-10 new cool WDs and ~5-10 sub-Gaia L/T dwarfs with parallaxes across ~27 deg^2; small numbers, but each is a secure individual discovery because the parallax itself is the proof. Gaia DR4 (2 Dec 2026) adds nothing here: these objects are below its magnitude limit.
data_sources: nsc_dr2.object (pmra/pmdec, ndet, deltamjd, class_star) for pre-selection, Data Lab TAP
nsc_dr2.meas (dated per-exposure ra/dec, mag, per band) + nsc_dr2.exposure (mjd, airmass, fwhm, depth) for the 5-parameter fits
DES DR2 / LS DR10 deep coadd griz(Y) colours; LS DR10 tractor forced unWISE W1/W2 (asset 8) for the IR-faint WD test
VISTA VIDEO (covers XMM-LSS=X, CDFS=C, ES1=E fields) and VHS J/H/Ks (asset 5) for L/T colours
Euclid Q1 EDF-F (= CDFS = DES C3) VIS+NISP catalogues via IRSA HATS/LSDB (public) for 0.1-arcsec morphology and Y/J/H
Gaia DR3 (control stars G=19-20.7), Gaia DR3/DES-SN quasar catalogue (Tie+2017) as zero-parallax control, CatWISE2020 + Gentile Fusillo+2021 WD catalogue for the novelty kill
selection: Fields: the 10 DES-SN pointings C1-3, E1-2, S1-2, X1-3 (~2.7 deg^2 usable each, ~27 deg^2; C3 and X3 are the deep fields with 3x400 s r and 11x330 s z per visit, visits every ~6 nights Aug-Feb for 5 seasons 2013-2018), COSMOS excluded (already done). Objects: NSC point sources with ndet >= 100 spanning >= 4 seasons, 21 < r < 24 (or 21 < z < 24 for red objects). Pre-select ~2x10^4 objects by (a) NSC object PM S/N > 3 or |PM| > 15 mas/yr, or (b) colour boxes: WD g-r < 0.7 & r-z < 0.6 (extend to r-z < 0 for CIA WDs) and no Gaia DR3 source within 2 arcsec after PM propagation; L/T i-z > 1.2 or z-J > 2.0. For each, fit alpha, delta, mu_alpha, mu_delta, parallax per band to the meas positions (with per-exposure zero-point nuisance terms and airmass < 1.5 cut); keep parallax/sigma >= 5, parallax >= 5 mas, and r/i/z parallaxes mutually consistent. Expected per-epoch precision 15-25 mas at r=22-23, so sigma_parallax ~1-2.5 mas with N~300, i.e. 5-sigma reach ~200 pc at r=21, ~140 pc at r=22, ~80 pc at r=23. Gate zero (lesson 10): recover Gaia DR3 parallaxes for >= 200 stars at G=19.5-20.7 in C3 to <= 2 mas rms, and get parallax = 0 within the floor for >= 500 DES-SN quasars, before any discovery claim.
main_false_positive_channel: Per-exposure astrometric systematics that correlate with the parallax factor: differential chromatic refraction (blue WDs / red L dwarfs) combined with the seasonal hour-angle pattern of DES-SN observing, DECam tree-ring and chip-edge distortions not captured by NSC's per-chip Gaia calibration, and centroid pulls from faint galaxies blended within the seeing disk. Also NSC object splitting for PM > ~0.3 arcsec/yr. Mitigations: per-band fits with cross-band consistency, quasar zero-parallax floor per field, airmass cut, Euclid/LS morphology to reject blends.
credit_channel: NOT VSX/TNS/MPC: an RNAAS note or AJ-style paper, ideally co-authored with a WD or brown-dwarf specialist (precedent: citizen scientist Frank Kiwy's 2021 RNAAS and 2022 AJ 'Discovery of 34 low-mass comoving systems using NSC DR2', written with Backyard Worlds professionals and press-released by NOIRLab). Objects enter SIMBAD via the publication. Direct consumers: the Gaia 100-pc WD census (Jimenez-Esteban / Gentile Fusillo), IR-faint WD spectroscopy programmes (Bergeron, Kilic), the Kirkpatrick 20-pc/UCD census.
why_not_already_done: The DES-SN collaboration used the deep coadds for SN hosts (Wiseman+2020) and quasar selection (Tie+2017) but never published stellar astrometry from the 5-season cadence; Bernstein+2017 characterised DECam astrometry as calibration, not as a discovery survey. NSC DR2 (Nidever+2021) fits proper motions only, with no parallax term, and nobody has refit its meas table. The one deep-field precedent, Fajardo-Acosta+2022 (JSP-II), measured proper motions (not parallaxes) in COSMOS with HST+HSC and stopped there. Kiwy/Backyard Worlds use NSC PMs to find red comoving companions of Gaia stars, not blind parallaxes of blue objects. The Euclid Consortium's Q1 papers (5,306 photometric UCD candidates in the EDFs, Zhang+2025; NISP spectra, Mohandasan+2025) explicitly defer parallaxes to Euclid's own monthly EDF visits, so EDF-F (=C3) astrometry will be consortium-owned around 2027-28; Rubin DDF parallaxes arrive with DR2 (~2028) and the user has no Rubin data rights. So the niche exists because it sits between what the survey teams bothered to publish and what the next-generation facilities will do automatically in ~2 years. Honest risk: an unpublished DES-internal astrometric catalogue could exist; an ADS/arXiv search for 'DES supernova fields proper motion parallax' is mandatory at gate zero.
session_lesson_exploited: Asset 6 (nsc_dr2.meas has dated per-exposure positions; ~800 r-band exposures per deg^2 in the DES-SN fields), lesson 10 (recover the pipeline's own template: Gaia stars and zero-parallax quasars on the identical configuration), asset 5 (VIDEO/VHS near-IR barely used so far), asset 8 (LS DR10 forced unWISE W1 > 19.3 as a free IR-faint test), lesson 12 (access checked: Rubin DP2 late-summer 2026 and DR1 Nov 2026 are data-rights gated; Euclid Q1 Mar 2025 / Q2 24 Jun 2026 are public on IRSA and Euclid DR1 is public 21 Oct 2026).
feasibility_notes: Data Lab TAP works without an account for sync queries and the user has already run thousands of NSC queries; meas volume is ~2x10^4 pre-selected objects x 300-1,400 rows = 6-30 M rows in chunked async queries (hours). Fitting is trivial least squares on the NUC. No IRSA rate-limit exposure. Archive-only confirmation is complete: parallax + colours + IR-faintness IS the discovery; spectroscopy is optional community follow-up. Euclid Q1 EDF-F products via public IRSA HATS/LSDB. Labor ~2-3 weeks including the control suite. Clock: usable until Rubin DR2 / Euclid EDF astrometry (~2028); DR4-proof.
novelty_per_labor_guess: MEDIUM-HIGH: ~10-20 individually secure new nearby objects (parallax-proven, individually novel, collectively an RNAAS/AJ set) for ~2-3 weeks of work; low competition for 12-18 months; the counts are small because the area is 27 deg^2, but the per-object certainty is the highest of the three lanes.

title: Appeared-and-stayed at matched depth: absent in every PS1 3pi epoch (2010-14, r>22.5), bright and constant in ZTF (2018-26, r<20.5)
what_we_would_find: Constant-bright NEW point sources with delta-r >= 2.5-4 mag between the PS1 era and the ZTF era that never produced a difference-image alert because they were already bright when the ZTF references were built (lesson 3). Three classes: (i) AGN that turned on between ~2014 and 2018 and stayed on (the J075308 archetype), a class no broker or ZTF-internal changing-look selection can produce; expected ~50-300 over ~20,000 deg^2 at dec > -28 (order-of-magnitude: ~6x10^5 ZTF r<20.5 AGN x a 10^-4 to 10^-3 per-decade rate of >2.5 mag turn-ons); (ii) Galactic objects at r=19-20.5 that ASAS-SN (V<17-18), ATLAS (o<19.5) and Gaia alerts (G<19) could not see: nova-likes/CVs in multi-year high states, post-outburst novae and FUor/EXor-type eruptions of 2014-2018, R CrB stars recovering from a PS1-era deep minimum; expected ~5-30 in |b|<15; (iii) bycatch: sub-Gaia PM > 0.2 arcsec/yr objects revealed by a colour-matched PS1 counterpart 2-10 arcsec away.
data_sources: ZTF DR24 object + light-curve HATS on IRSA S3 (asset 7, anonymous access) read with lsdb/dask
PS1 DR2 mean/object-thin HATS at data.lsdb.io (public; the NASA Fornax 'Cross-Match ZTF and Pan-STARRS using LSDB' notebook is a ready template)
