PS1 DR2 Detection table via the MAST catalogs API (account-free, per position) for per-epoch absence 2010-2014; ps1images stack cutouts with mask/weight for coverage proof (lesson 9)
unTimely / unWISE epochal W1-W2 (2010-2020) and LS DR10 forced unWISE (asset 8) to date the turn-on in the mid-IR and to colour-classify AGN (W1-W2 > 0.8)
Gaia DR3 (phot_variable_flag, QSO/galaxy classifiers), CatWISE2020, ZTF forced photometry (ZFPS, works via the TU Delft address) for the difference-image flatness test
DESI DR1 / SDSS / LAMOST spectra where coverage is proven; VSX/TNS/SIMBAD/Gaia-alerts/CRTS/ATLAS for the multi-catalogue novelty gate
selection: Sky: PS1 x ZTF overlap, dec > -28, all latitudes, with a local PS1 completeness gate (>= 5 PS1 objects at 21.5 < r < 22.5 within 30 arcsec, otherwise drop; this removes the confusion-limited inner plane, |b| < ~3-5). ZTF side (bright, robust end): zr median 17.0-20.5, >= 30 detections on >= 15 nights spanning >= 3 yr, catflags = 0, per-epoch centroid rms < 0.3 arcsec with centroid-vs-magnitude slope consistent with zero (asset 4, kills blends and ghosts), 2018-2026 centroid drift < 0.4 arcsec (PM < 50 mas/yr), measured-mag-vs-limitmag slope ~0 (asset 4). PS1 side (absence): no PS1 DR2 object within 1.5 arcsec in any of grizy (stack or single epoch), no Detection-table entry within 2 arcsec on >= 8 distinct PS1 epochs spanning >= 2 yr, local stack 5-sigma limit >= 22.5. Expected funnel: ~10^8 ZTF sources -> ~10^3-10^4 raw non-matches -> ~200-500 after coverage and ghost gates -> ~50-300 genuine 'appeared' objects, then classified by unWISE colour/rise, Gaia classifiers and spectra where they exist.
main_false_positive_channel: False absence: PS1 mask holes around bright stars, chip gaps in low-epoch skycells, and crowding incompleteness in the plane (the coverage gate and the neighbour-count test are mandatory). False presence: ZTF ghosts/crosstalk near bright stars and asteroids/high-PM objects (killed by the >= 15-night fixed-centroid rule and the drift test). Astrophysical mimics: Miras/SRVs whose PS1 epochs all fell near minimum (killed by requiring absence on >= 8 PS1 epochs over >= 2 yr, and by unWISE: Miras are W1-bright and stable-red).
credit_channel: Galactic branch -> VSX (named credit; CV/N/FU/RCB types), plus AAVSO/ATel-level notes for anything bright; AGN branch -> TNS AstroNote or an RNAAS sample note (refereed/co-authored per the publication policy), with the per-object dating figure (PS1 absent -> unWISE rise -> flat ZTF) as the deliverable and spectroscopy left to DESI/4MOST-adjacent contacts. Note honestly: the AGN branch has no codified credit registry.
why_not_already_done: The ZTF changing-look AGN groups (Graham+, Frederick+, Ricci/Trakhtenbrot) select on variability inside ZTF or on spectroscopic pairs; a source that was already bright and flat at the ZTF reference epoch has neither alerts nor ZTF-internal variability, so it is invisible to them (lesson 3). VASCO (Villarroel+) compares USNO-B/POSS to PS1: older, shallower and the opposite direction. PS1 was treated by everyone as the reference catalogue, not as an earlier epoch to be tested for absence, and until LSDB/HATS distribution (2025) a 10^8 x 10^9 crossmatch was a cluster job, not a NUC job. Relation to the CLOSED turn-on lane (explicit): same physical class, but (1) the early epoch is the uniform 12-epoch PS1 3pi stack covering ~15,000 deg^2 of northern sky where NSC has no DECam data, and (2) the selection is inverted to start from the S/N>10, >=15-night ZTF end and require ABSENCE in the deep epoch, so a candidate cannot be created by a blend (it would need >= 6 unresolved r>22.5 stars), by cosmic rays or by sub-threshold noise, which is exactly what the structural lesson demanded. If the in-progress corrected re-run already inverted the selection, this lane reduces to extending it to the PS1-north footprint and should be merged, not run twice. Hard clock: Gaia DR4 epoch photometry (2 Dec 2026) exposes the G<20.7 subset to DPAC variability and changing-look miners.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 3 (constant-bright new sources are structurally invisible to every broker; only a static cross-epoch comparison finds them), lesson 1 (absence relative to expected coverage is information), asset 4 (ZTF per-epoch centroid and limitmag slope as blend/artifact killers), lesson 9 (prove PS1 coverage before citing absence), asset 7 (bulk HATS instead of the ~1,100-query IRSA per-position ceiling), asset 8 (unWISE forced photometry as free contemporaneous mid-IR).
feasibility_notes: Bulk stage: lsdb crossmatch of ZTF DR24 object HATS (IRSA S3, anonymous) against PS1 DR2 HATS (data.lsdb.io), column-filtered to r < 20.5 and nobs >= 30; TB-scale streaming but partition-parallel, days on the 6-core NUC or batched per HEALPix. Per-candidate stage: MAST PS1 detection API (~1 call/s, 10^3-10^4 calls, hours), ps1images cutouts, unTimely via IRSA TAP upload (avoid per-position rate limits). Archive-only confirmation is possible for the 'appeared and stayed' fact (PS1 absence + PS1 coverage proof + ZTF presence + unWISE rise); physical class from colours/WISE/existing spectra; spectroscopic confirmation by the community. The same infrastructure runs the 'vanished' direction (PS1 present r<21, ZTF absent to limitmag with >= 15 visits) as a follow-on. Labor ~2-4 weeks including the crossmatch build.
novelty_per_labor_guess: MEDIUM-HIGH for the AGN branch (tens to hundreds of objects of a class no pipeline produces; sample-level novelty), MEDIUM for the Galactic branch (few objects but VSX-creditable and individually interesting); ~3 weeks of labor, most of it reusable.

title: Sub-Gaia reduced-proper-motion census of the DECam south (dec < -30): cool, IR-faint and halo white dwarfs beyond Gaia's limit from NSC DR2 proper motions
what_we_would_find: The first white-dwarf sample below the Gaia limit over the ~8,000 deg^2 of DES+DELVE sky south of dec -30 where no faint proper-motion catalogue exists (GPS1+ stops at dec -30): ~3,000-8,000 new WD candidates at 20.7 < r < 22.5 (170-400 pc) selected by NSC DR2 proper motions (PM > 40 mas/yr at S/N > 8) in the reduced-proper-motion diagram with DES/DELVE/LS DR10 colours. The individually novel tail: ~100-150 ultracool WDs (T_eff < 4,000 K, r-z < 0.1 from collision-induced absorption, unWISE W1 > 19.3 'IR-faint'), comparable to the entire known IR-faint WD sample (~100, Bergeron+2022); ~100-250 halo-kinematics WDs (PM > 140 mas/yr at 300 pc, v_tan > 200 km/s); and the 'too fast' tail from a split-object test (PM > 0.3 arcsec/yr objects that NSC fragments into 2+ entries with disjoint MJD ranges): nearby (< 50 pc) ultracool WDs and late-T dwarfs that both Gaia and CatWISE missed. Gaia DR4 does not reach these magnitudes.
data_sources: nsc_dr2.object (pmra, pmdec, pmraerr, pmdecerr, ndet, deltamjd, class_star, gmag/rmag/zmag) via Data Lab TAP
nsc_dr2.meas for the top ~200 candidates (dated refits, split-object verification, parallax attempt for the nearest)
DELVE DR2 / DES DR2 griz and LS DR10 tractor (type = PSF; forced unWISE W1/W2 through NEOWISE year 7, asset 8)
VHS DR5/6 J/Ks via ESO/VizieR TAP (asset 5) for the IR-faint confirmation

Gaia DR3 (negative crossmatch after PM propagation; the EDR3 100-pc WD sample at 19.5 < G < 20.7 as the recovery control), Gentile Fusillo+2021 WD catalogue + its RPM extension, CatWISE2020 motion catalogue, SIMBAD (multi-catalogue novelty gate)
Gaia DR3 QSO candidates / LS DR10 QSO colours at 21 < r < 22.5 as the zero-proper-motion control that calibrates the false high-PM rate
selection: Footprint: NSC DR2 at dec < -30 and |b| > 10 (DES ~5,000 deg^2 + DELVE, ~8,000 deg^2 total), excluding the LMC/SMC/Sgr cores. Objects: class_star > 0.8 (and LS DR10 type PSF where covered), 20.7 < r < 22.5, ndet >= 15 over deltamjd >= 3 yr (DES baselines 2013-2019), PM S/N > 8 and PM > 40 mas/yr (NSC per-epoch ~40 mas at r=22 over ~40 detections gives sigma_PM ~3-5 mas/yr). WD box: H_r = r + 5 log10(mu[arcsec/yr]) + 5 >= 15.5, g-r < 0.8, r-z < 0.6 (extending to r-z < 0). Ultracool sub-box: r-z < 0.1 and unWISE W1 > 19.3 (coverage proven per object, lesson 9). Halo sub-box: PM > 140 mas/yr. Split-object test: pairs of NSC objects within 4 arcsec, |delta r| < 0.3 mag, disjoint MJD ranges, implied PM > 300 mas/yr. Controls (lesson 10): (a) recover >= 90% of Gaia-EDR3 100-pc WDs at 19.5 < G < 20.7 in the footprint from NSC PMs alone; (b) >= 10^4 faint QSOs must give PM consistent with zero; their tail sets the spurious PM > 40 mas/yr rate (expected ~10^-4, i.e. ~50-100 contaminants over ~10^6 faint compact sources, removed by colour and W1-W2). Expected output: ~10^6 rows after the PM cut, ~10^4 in the WD box, ~200 individually interesting.
main_false_positive_channel: Underestimated NSC proper-motion errors at the faint end (magnitude- and colour-dependent centroiding, DCR, detections clustered into two seasons so one bad measurement gets large leverage) inflating the high-PM tail; unresolved blends and compact galaxies passing class_star > 0.8; RPM contamination by cool halo subdwarfs (mitigated by colour, sdMs have g-r > 1, and by unWISE, sdMs have W1 < 17). Both controls quantify the contamination directly on the pipeline's own configuration.
credit_channel: NOT VSX/TNS/MPC: a catalogue paper or RNAAS with a WD co-author (Kiwy 2022 AJ shows amateur-led NSC DR2 astrometry papers are accepted and press-released by NOIRLab); objects enter SIMBAD via publication. Direct consumers: the 4MOST white-dwarf survey (southern, operations from 2026), Kilic/Bergeron Gemini-South IR-faint WD spectroscopy, Gentile Fusillo catalogue updates, halo WD kinematics work.
why_not_already_done: GPS1+ (Tian+2020) delivered 19 < r < 22.5 proper motions for 400 M sources but only where PS1/SDSS exist (dec > -30), so the DES/DELVE south is a proper-motion desert below G = 20.7. The WD community (Gentile Fusillo, Jimenez-Esteban, Kilic, Bergeron) works from Gaia: their RPM extension (~10,200 objects) is Gaia-based. The DES collaboration's WD work was photometric and Y6 Gold carries Gaia proper motions, not internal ones; a search found no DES/DELVE stellar PM catalogue. The NSC team (Nidever+2021) advertised faint-WD proper motions as a DR2 use case and did not follow up. Backyard Worlds / Kiwy use NSC PMs but start from WISE-bright red UCD candidates; cool WDs are precisely the WISE-faint blue objects their pipeline never sees. Rubin DR1 (Nov 2026, ~6 months baseline, data-rights gated) cannot measure 40 mas/yr; DR2/3 (~2028-29) will, so the window is ~2 years. Honest caveats: an unpublished DES-internal PM catalogue could exist; an arXiv search for a 2025-26 'DELVE/NSC faint white dwarf proper motion' paper is mandatory at gate zero; the product is a population plus ~200 individually interesting objects, not one spectacular object.
session_lesson_exploited: Asset 6 (NSC object table = averaged astrometry incl. PM; meas for dated refits and the split-object check), asset 8 (LS DR10 forced unWISE gives the IR-faint test for free, no IRSA per-position load), asset 5 (VHS J/Ks), lesson 10 (template recovery on the pipeline's own configuration plus a zero-PM quasar control), lesson 9 (prove LS DR10/VHS coverage per object before quoting W1 or J limits), and the multi-catalogue novelty gate (Gaia + GF21 + CatWISE + SIMBAD, not SIMBAD-only).
feasibility_notes: Pure catalogue-level SQL on Data Lab (account-free; NSC access already proven this project); pre-cut ~10^6 rows, final ~10^4; VHS via ESO/VizieR TAP bulk; unWISE via ls_dr10.tractor on Data Lab; compute trivial on the NUC. Archive-only confirmation is the field standard for WD candidates (Kilic+2006, Harris+2006 were SDSS+USNO-B catalogue papers): PM + RPM + colours + IR-faintness. A subset with ndet > 40 gets a meas-level parallax attempt (sigma ~5-8 mas, i.e. only < 50 pc objects, which is exactly the split-object tail). Spectroscopy is the community's part (4MOST, Gemini). Labor ~1-2 weeks of SQL plus the control suite; DR4-proof; ~2-year window before Rubin proper motions.
novelty_per_labor_guess: HIGH on population count (thousands of new-to-knowledge objects for ~1-2 weeks of work) and MEDIUM per object, with ~200 individually interesting ultracool/halo candidates; lowest labor of the three lanes and it shares its NSC infrastructure with lane 1.

title: Parallax veto on non-thermal AGN-candidate catalogues (gamma-ray / radio / hard-X-ray 'blazars' and 'quasars' that are Galactic)
what_we_would_find: Galactic non-thermal emitters that are filed as blazars/AGN because they sit in AGN colour boxes and were associated with radio, gamma-ray or hard-X-ray sources without an astrometric check: AR Sco-type white-dwarf pulsars and magnetic propellers (AR Sco itself has AllWISE W1-W2 = 0.81, W2-W3 = 2.57, i.e. the Stern/blazar-strip box, with Gaia parallax 8.54 mas and 5-9 mJy in VLASS/RACS, measured today), spider MSP binaries hiding inside 4FGL 'bcu' associations, symbiotic X-ray binaries and intermediate polars among the 88%-'extragalactic' eRASS:3 hard-band counterparts, plus whatever does not fit any class. Each survivor is a new-to-knowledge Galactic object (a gamma-ray or radio-loud binary), not a bookkeeping fix.
data_sources: 4FGL-DR4 (7,194 sources; 1,625 BCU + ~2,300 bll/fsrq association counterparts with arcsec positions; FSSC/VizieR)
WIBRaLS2 (9,541) + KDEBLLACS (5,579) WISE blazar-like radio-loud sources, |b|>10 (VizieR J/ApJS/242/4)
Assef+2018 AllWISE R90 AGN catalogue (4.5M) and CatWISE2020 colours
Gaia DR3 qso_candidates (6.6M, ~52% purity; gaiadr3.qso_candidates / VizieR I/356/qsocand) + gaiadr3.gaia_source astrometry (parallax, pm, ruwe)
RACS-low2 Stokes I (3.92M sources, Dec<=+48, 195 uJy rms, released Jun 2026, CASDA) and VLASS QL Epochs 1-3 (Dec>-40, ~120 uJy rms, CIRADA/NRAO via CADC)

eROSITA-DE DR2 eRASS:3 main (1,911,744 point sources) + hard 2.3-5 keV catalogue (~15,000) + its six counterpart catalogues (released 31 Jul 2026, erodat bulk download); 5XMM-DR15 hard-band detections (released 9 Jun 2026)

Novelty gates: SIMBAD, VSX, Gaia DR3 vari classes, Marton+2023 YSOs, HASH PNe, Akras+2019/Merc+2019 symbiotic lists, SRSC (839 radio stars) and Yiu+2024 VLASS-Gaia radio stars, ATNF pulsars, Ritter-Kolb
selection: Union of four branches, all requiring Gaia DR3 parallax_over_error >= 5 AND (pm/pm_error >= 5 OR parallax >= 1 mas), ruwe < 1.4, G < 20, |b| > 10 deg, LS DR10/PS1 type = PSF. (A) 4FGL-DR4 blazar association counterparts within 1.5 arcsec of a Gaia source: ~3,900 counterparts x chance rate 5,000 deg^-2 x pi(1.5")^2 = 2.7e-3 -> ~10 chance Gaia matches, ~2-3 with 5-sigma parallax by chance; anything else is real. (B) WIBRaLS2+KDEBLLACS within 2 arcsec: ~73 chance matches, ~18 with significant parallax by chance; the papers' own >12% non-blazar-like fraction implies ~1,800 non-blazars, of which an estimated 200-400 are Galactic; after known-class removal expect 50-100 objects to vet. (C) R90 AGN (W1-W2 >= 0.8 Vega) x RACS-low2/VLASS within 3 arcsec x parallax: chance 115 deg^-2 x pi(3")^2 = 2.5e-4 per object; the AR Sco control must survive this branch. (D) Gaia qso_candidates x eRASS:3 hard-band (15k) or 5XMM hard detections within 3-sigma X-ray error, parallax >= 5 sigma: expect 30-100 objects, dominated by IPs/symbiotic-X/quiescent HMXBs if real. Vetting per object: WISE 6-arcsec blend check with LS DR10 cutouts, radio-position vs Gaia PM-propagated position at radio epoch, ZTF/ATLAS/TESS light curve for period < 1 d or outbursts, GALEX UV excess, eRASS/XMM hardness. Target output: 5-30 uncatalogued Galactic non-thermal binaries; the gamma-ray branch yield is probably 0-5 but each would be a Galactic gamma-ray binary.
main_false_positive_channel: Chance superposition: a foreground Gaia star inside the 6-arcsec WISE beam or 10-25 arcsec RACS beam of a genuine background AGN inherits the AGN's colours/radio flux. Killed by LS DR10 resolved-morphology inspection, unWISE 2.75-arcsec coadds, VLASS 2.5-arcsec positions, and PM-propagated positional offsets at the radio epoch. Second channel: spurious Gaia parallaxes of blended/duplicated sources (ruwe, duplicated_source, ipd_gof flags). Third: objects that are known but only in VSX/ZTF-periodic catalogues rather than SIMBAD - the novelty gate must be multi-catalogue.
credit_channel: VSX for anything showing periodic or eruptive optical variability (named credit; add X-ray/radio/gamma association in remarks); TNS AstroNote for a Galactic identification of a 4FGL/eROSITA-hard source; community-confirm by Fermi/radio/CV spectroscopists (Strader/Swihart for spiders, Pelisoli/Marsh for WD pulsars, Rodriguez/Galiullin for CVs). No telescope needed: the discovery claim is the astrometric-physical contradiction plus archival light curves.
why_not_already_done: The Fermi-LAT catalogue team (Ballet, Abdollahi, Burnett) associates via likelihood ratio against radio/WISE lists and never vetoes with Gaia astrometry (one-off cases like 4FGL J0647.7-4418 show the contradiction is discovered only by accident). D'Abrusco/Massaro built WIBRaLS2/KDEBLLACS to find blazars and treat the >12% non-blazar-like fraction as contamination, not as targets. Flesch (Milliquas v8) and Storey-Fisher (Quaia) and Fu (CatNorth/CatSouth) DID apply Gaia proper-motion cuts - but they discard the rejects unpublished, so Milliquas/Quaia themselves are dead as inputs and only the never-cleaned catalogues (4FGL, WIBRaLS2, R90, raw qso_candidates, eRASS:3 counterpart classes) remain. Pelisoli+2025 searched Gaia+WISE for AR Sco analogues but only inside the HRD bridge (56 candidates, 1 new pulsar); the radio-star cataloguers (Driessen SRSC, Yiu VLASS-Gaia) start from Gaia stars and never look at AGN catalogues. Verified today: AR Sco is absent from Gaia qso_candidates, WIBRaLS2 and Milliquas despite AGN colours, which shows the catalogue-membership branches (A,B,D) are incomplete and branch (C) is required.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 9 (prove coverage before a null: RACS-low2 stops at Dec +48, VLASS at -40, LoTSS is 27% of the north); lesson 10 (template controls: AR Sco must be recovered by branch C, Object B 3161546596480983040 - Gaia QSOC 'AGN' overturned by 5.3-sigma parallax - by the qso_candidates branch); lesson 11 (VSX/TNS channels, community-confirm); the multi-catalogue novelty gate lesson from the Gaia campaign (SIMBAD-only gates rejected 13/13 true candidates once).
feasibility_notes: All inputs are anonymous: Gaia archive TAP, VizieR TAP (4FGL, WIBRaLS2, R90, qsocand confirmed reachable today), CASDA/CADC for RACS-low2 and VLASS QL, erodat bulk FITS for eROSITA DR2, HEASARC/XCAT-DB for 5XMM-DR15. Crossmatches are TOPCAT/astropy on a laptop (largest table 6.6M rows). Vetting labour ~10 min/object for ~100-200 objects. Archive-only confirmation is possible for the periodic/variable ones (ZTF/ATLAS/TESS periods + GALEX + radio position); spectroscopic class needs the community. What changed vs the dead eRASS1 lane: this is not an X-ray-selected accretor search on Gaia counterparts; it is a catalogue-contradiction search whose X-ray branch uses the new eRASS:3 hard band and the counterpart classes released 31 Jul 2026. Gaia DR4 (2 Dec 2026) will tighten G>19 parallaxes and should be used to re-run the veto.
novelty_per_labor_guess: Medium-high: labour is days of crossmatching plus ~100-200 object vettings; expected 5-30 uncatalogued Galactic non-thermal objects, with a few possible high-value outcomes (gamma-ray binary, WD pulsar) whose novelty per object is far above a routine CV.

title: Beyond-Gaia X-ray counterparts: faint, blue, W1-dark, variable point sources at 5XMM-DR15 / CSC 2.1 / eRASS:3 positions
what_we_would_find: Galactic accretors whose optical counterpart is 20.5 < r < 23 - below Gaia astrometry and below ZTF's per-epoch limit - and therefore absent from every Gaia-anchored X-ray CV search of 2024-2026: faint magnetic CVs and dwarf novae at 1-5 kpc (thick-disc/halo population, X-ray selection favours polars/IPs), AM CVn systems, quiescent LMXBs, and possibly isolated neutron stars or ultracompact binaries with faint optical counterparts. In the counterpart pipelines these sources are filed as 'extragalactic' by default because a faint blue point source with X-rays looks like an AGN until you notice it has no mid-IR flux and varies like a star.
data_sources: 5XMM-DR15 (released 9 Jun 2026; ~1.1M unique sources over ~1,400 deg^2; positions ~1.5 arcsec) and its stacked catalogue
Chandra Source Catalog 2.1 (~400k unique sources; 0.5-1 arcsec positions; existing NWAY crossmatch to Gaia DR3 / LS DR10 / PS1 / 2MASS gives 229k counterparts of 389k)
eROSITA-DE DR2 eRASS:3 main catalogue (1.91M point sources, ~4 arcsec 1-sigma positions, ~3e-14 cgs) plus eRASS1 DR1 for eRASS1-vs-eRASS:3 flux change
Legacy Surveys DR10 south (Dec < +32; r ~ 23.5-24; type PSF; forced unWISE W1/W2 through NEOWISE year 7, W1 > ~19.3 Vega non-detection limit) via Astro Data Lab TAP
NSC DR2 nsc_dr2.meas per-exposure photometry (DES wide ~10 r epochs; DES SN deep fields C/X/E/S ~800 r epochs per deg^2; DECaLS 3-6) via Data Lab
ZTF DR light curves (censored to detections; sparse bright detections = outbursts) via IRSA per-position (<1,100 queries) or the HATS/S3 bulk endpoint

GALEX GUVcat (UV excess), VHS/VVV/UKIDSS J/K (donor star and distance), Gaia DR3 (to prove the source is NOT there), Euclid Q2 (24 Jun 2026) / DR1 (21 Oct 2026) 0.16-arcsec morphology where fields overlap (EDF-F sits on the DES C fields)
selection: X-ray source at |b| > 15 deg inside LS DR10 south; LS DR10 PSF counterpart within 1 arcsec (CSC), 2 arcsec (XMM) or 3-sigma (eRASS) with 20.5 < r < 23.0; no Gaia DR3 five-parameter solution within 1.5 arcsec; forced W1 S/N < 3 or r - W1(Vega) < 3.0 (AGN at these magnitudes have r - W1 = 4-6, so W1-darkness kills AGN robustly for r <= 22.5; the 22.5-23 tail is flagged lower-confidence); g - r < 0.6; F_X(0.2-2.3 or 0.5-2 keV)/F_r > 0.1 (coronal stars < 0.01). Variability from any of: NSC meas >= 6 r-band epochs with rms > 0.2 mag or range > 0.8 mag after the slope-vs-limitmag test (slope ~0 real, ~1 threshold artefact) and per-epoch centroid within 1 arcsec; ZTF sparse detections (<= 5 rows, r < 19.5) at a position whose LS DR10 mag is > 2 mag fainter (outburst caught by a censored light curve); XMM var_flag or eRASS1 -> eRASS:3 flux ratio > 3. Expected funnel for 5XMM+CSC: ~600k sources in footprint -> ~240k with faint PSF counterparts -> ~15k W1-dark -> ~7k blue -> ~3k with F_X/F_r > 0.1 -> ~300-600 variable (multi-epoch data exist over ~40% of the area) -> visual vetting -> 30-100 real Galactic accretors, ~70% uncatalogued. eRASS:3 leg adds ~15,000 deg^2 at 95 sources/deg^2 (CVs with L_X > 1e31 visible to ~1.7 kpc, r ~ 21-22.5) but its 4-arcsec positions put ~1 faint LS source in every error circle, so it only counts when blue + W1-dark + variable all hold; expect ~100-200 additional candidates, chance-dominated before vetting.
main_false_positive_channel: Chance alignment of a faint blue variable (RR Lyrae at 50 kpc, flare star, faint AGN) with an X-ray source whose true counterpart is a fainter/extended AGN - worst for eRASS (~4 arcsec) and tolerable for CSC (~0.7 arcsec: <1% chance at r < 24). Second: low-luminosity or z > 3 AGN that are genuinely W1-dark at r ~ 22.5-23 (contained by the r <= 22.5 core sample and by requiring stellar-type variability - outbursts, eclipses, periods - not stochastic 0.2-mag AGN jitter). Third: NSC/DECam systematics (bad epochs, blends): the session's slope-vs-limitmag and centroid tests are mandatory, and the DECam-caught faint state of ZTF19abxfaon is the positive control for the NSC leg.
credit_channel: VSX (new CV / AM CVn / X-ray binary with light-curve type and X-ray association; named credit, one filing already done this way), TNS AstroNote for exotica (qLMXB, INS-with-counterpart, ultracompact candidates); community-confirm spectroscopy by the eROSITA/Chandra CV groups (Rodriguez, Galiullin, Schwope) who are natural consumers of a 'faint tail' list they cannot reach with Gaia.
why_not_already_done: Every 2024-2026 X-ray CV search is Gaia-anchored by construction: Rodriguez's X-ray main sequence (XMM x Gaia 2024, CSC 2.1 x Gaia - e.g. 2CXO J050740.7-091337 at 18-20 mag, May 2026; volume-limited 150-1000 pc), Galiullin+2024 (CSC x Gaia, 14 new) and Galiullin+2025 (eROSITA/XMM/Swift/ROSAT x Gaia HRD bridge, 444 candidates), Schwope+2024 (eRASS1 CVs), Munoz-Giraldo+2025 (period bouncers) - all need a parallax to place the object on the HRD, so r > 20.5 is invisible to them. Salvato's NWAY counterpart catalogues (eRASS:3, CSC 2.1) assign 'extragalactic' to faint PSF sources with no Gaia astrometry and classify rather than chase; Yang+2022 MUWCLASS needs Gaia/2MASS/WISE features and calls W1-dark faint sources unclassifiable; INS hunters (Kurpas, Rigoselli, Demasi) demand NO counterpart to r ~ 24; DES/XXL/Stripe-82X teams target AGN. What changed vs the dead eRASS1 accretor lane: that lane required a Gaia counterpart and used F_X/F_opt on Gaia photometry; this lane lives entirely in the 20.5-23 mag bin, uses two catalogues that did not exist then (5XMM-DR15 Jun 2026, eROSITA DR2 Jul 2026), and its discriminators are the three session levers (NSC per-exposure light curves, LS forced W1 as an AGN killer, censored-ZTF outburst rows).
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 1 (ZTF lists only detections: <= 5 bright rows at a faint LS position is an outburst signature); lesson 4 (per-epoch centroid and mag-vs-limitmag slope separate real sources from threshold artefacts); lesson 6 (nsc_dr2.meas dated exposures; DES SN fields ~800 r exposures per deg^2); lesson 8 (LS DR10 forced WISE is a NEOWISE-year-7 unWISE coadd giving W1 > 19.3 for free); lesson 5 (VHS J gives the donor-star distance); lesson 9 (prove LS/NSC/ZTF coverage at each position before citing a null); lesson 10 (recover known faint CVs on the pipeline's own configuration first).
feasibility_notes: CSC 2.1 (CXC TAP), 5XMM-DR15 (XCAT-DB/HEASARC), eROSITA DR2 (erodat bulk FITS), LS DR10 and NSC meas (Data Lab anonymous TAP, batch the cone queries - single-position loops were what tripped IRSA at ~1,100) are all account-free. ZTF: per-position IRSA for < 1,000 objects, HATS/S3 bulk beyond. Compute is laptop-scale; the expensive step is ~300-600 visual vettings (~5 min each) plus ~30-100 VSX write-ups. Archive-only confirmation is genuinely possible for CVs (outbursts, periods, X-ray/optical ratio, UV excess, W1-darkness) - VSX does not require spectra. Control set: VSX 'UG'/'AM' objects with quiescent r > 20.5 inside the XMM/Chandra footprints (expect a few dozen); require >= 80% recovery before any absence claim. Euclid DR1 (21 Oct 2026) adds sub-arcsec morphology on ~1,900 deg^2; Gaia DR4 (2 Dec 2026) will move the Gaia edge to G ~ 21 and should be used to re-cut the bin.
novelty_per_labor_guess: Medium-high and the most predictable of the three: tens of uncatalogued faint X-ray CVs per few weeks of work, each a VSX filing, with a small chance (a few percent of survivors) of an AM CVn, qLMXB or INS-with-counterpart.

title: Radio-loud short-period binaries: radio-star catalogues x sub-day optical periods, and WD+M catalogues x Stokes V/I radio
what_we_would_find: Magnetic white-dwarf binaries that emit radio: pre-polars and AR Sco-type WD pulsars (2-3 known), magnetic propellers, and the WD+M dwarf hosts of long-period radio transients (ILT J1101+5521, GLEAM-X J0704-37, ASKAP J1745-5051 class; theory papers put 100-1000 such systems within 2 kpc). The mismatch: a 'radio star' or 'M dwarf' in the radio-star catalogues that has a UV/XP white-dwarf component and an orbital period < 6 h, or a WD+M binary in the new Gaia-XP WDMS catalogue that sits on a circularly polarised or persistent radio source. Each is a new-to-knowledge object class member, filable to VSX once the optical period is measured.
data_sources: RACS-low2 (Jun 2026; Dec <= +48; 3.92M Stokes I sources, 195/163 uJy rms in I/V, 14-arcsec PSF; 221 Stokes V detections = 61 stars, 85 pulsars, 43 AGN/leakage, 1 unassociated; CASDA)

RACS-mid Stokes I (VizieR J/other/PASA/41.3), VLASS QL Epochs 1-3 (Dec > -40; E1 via VizieR J/ApJS/255/30, E2 CIRADA, E3 NRAO; 2.5-arcsec positions), LoTSS DR2 (4.4M sources, 5,634 deg^2, 83 uJy, 6 arcsec; VizieR J/A+A/659/A1) and V-LoTSS (68 V sources)
Sydney Radio Star Catalogue (839 stars; Driessen+2024) and Yiu+2024 VLASS/LoTSS-Gaia radio stars (65 VLASS + LoTSS stars within 500 pc)

Li+2025 Gaia-XP WDMS catalogue (~30,000 candidates within 1 kpc, ~1,700 high-confidence, strongest exactly for M-dwarf-dominated systems; ApJS 279, 47 - verify the table is public) and the 2025 Gaia+GALEX unresolved-WDMS catalogue

ZTF periodic-variable catalogues (Chen+2020, 781k), Gaia DR3 vari_eclipsing (2.2M), TESS (the ~4,400 cached EB light curves), GALEX GUVcat, Gaia DR3 astrometry, ATNF pulsar catalogue, VSX/Ritter-Kolb for known CVs
selection: Branch A (forward): union of catalogued radio stars (~2,500 objects) with Gaia parallax >= 5 sigma; compute L_nu = 4 pi d^2 S at 0.9/1.4/3 GHz; keep L_nu > 3e15 erg/s/Hz (about 10x above the Guedel-Benz coronal envelope for L_X ~ 1e29) OR Stokes V fraction > 30%; require an optical period < 0.5 d (ZTF/Gaia/TESS Lomb-Scargle on the full light curve, GALEX NUV excess or XP WD component as a second flag); drop W UMa contact binaries (EW class, no UV excess), known CVs, ATNF pulsars and RS CVn (P > 0.5 d). Expected 20-60 objects to vet, 1-5 novel. Branch B (reverse): 30k WDMS + UV-excess M dwarfs against RACS-low2 I/V (5-arcsec match; chance 115 deg^-2 x pi(5")^2 = 2.2e-4 -> ~7 chance matches), VLASS E1-3 (2.5 arcsec; 9e-5 -> ~3 chance) and LoTSS DR2 (3 arcsec over the ~9k northern targets; 1.7e-3 -> ~15 chance): ~25 chance matches total, all removable by PM-propagated offsets and cutout inspection; expected real persistent emitters 0-3 (Pelisoli+2024b found 0 secure in 846k WDs x VLASS E1, but that input excludes M-dwarf-dominated systems by construction). Branch C (phase 2, if A/B are null): forced Stokes-V photometry at the 30k WDMS positions in LoTSS DR2 and RACS-low2 mosaics via cutout services, 5-sigma threshold (0.13% x 30k = 40 false 3-sigma hits, ~0 at 5 sigma), because sporadic LPT emission is diluted below the catalogue thresholds.
main_false_positive_channel: Ordinary coronal/flare emission from the M dwarf itself (active M dwarfs are the dominant V-polarised radio stars, so a WD companion plus a short period are the only discriminators), chance alignment inside 14-25 arcsec RACS beams with background AGN (killed by VLASS 2.5-arcsec positions where Dec > -40 and by PM offsets), VLASS QL flux errors (~15%) and inter-epoch variability mistaken for astrophysical change, and W UMa systems that are genuinely radio-loud. Honest limit verified today: both known WD+M LPTs are catalogue-invisible in Stokes I - GLEAM-X J0704-37 (07:04:13.19 -37:06:14.3; Gaia G = 20.78, parallax -0.22 +/- 0.98 mas) has no RACS-low DR1, RACS-mid or VLASS E1 entry within 30 arcsec, and ILT J1101+5521 has no LoTSS DR2 entry at its position (the nearest, ILTJ110148.54+552110.0 at 0.70 mJy, 19 arcsec away, has no Gaia or GALEX counterpart within 4-5 arcsec and is unrelated). Only persistent emitters are recoverable by catalogue crossmatch (AR Sco: VLASS 5.4 mJy, RACS-low 8.6, RACS-mid 8.1; ASKAP J1745-5051: RACS-mid 22.4 mJy); J1912-4410 at ~0.5 mJy is below RACS. So branches A/B reach the AR Sco/ASKAP J1745 class only; the sporadic class needs branch C.
credit_channel: VSX for the optical periodicity (reflection/ellipsoidal/pulsed modulation; note the radio association and 'AR Sco-like' in remarks - named credit, archive-only), TNS AstroNote for the radio-loud WD-binary identification; community-confirm by the LPT/WD-pulsar groups (Hurley-Walker, Callingham/de Ruiter, Murphy/Pritchard, Pelisoli/Marsh) who have MeerKAT/ASKAP/LOFAR time and are actively asking for optical-first candidates.
why_not_already_done: The radio-first groups (GLEAM-X, V-LoTSS, RACS-V/VAST, CHIME) find pulses in images and only then look for optical counterparts; they do not start from WD+M lists. Pelisoli's group ran the two obvious reverse searches - 846k Gaia WDs x VLASS E1 (0 secure) and Gaia-bridge+WISE AR Sco analogues (56 candidates, 1 new pulsar, 10 YSOs, 7 CVs) - and both exclude M-dwarf-dominated PCEBs, which is exactly what ILT J1101 and GLEAM-X J0704 are. The radio-star cataloguers (Driessen SRSC, Yiu VLASS-Gaia, Pritchard RACS-V) classify by SIMBAD type and list 'M dwarf' or 'unknown' without testing for a WD component or a sub-day period. The population papers (2604.18688; 2509.09224) call for this search but do modelling. Both key inputs are new: the XP-WDMS catalogue (Jan 2025, published 2025) and RACS-low2 with its V catalogue (Jun 2026). Risk: the RACS-low2 authors may already have noticed an obvious WD+M among their 61 V-stars, and Branch A's residue may be mostly W UMa.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 9 (prove coverage: VLASS Dec > -40, RACS-low2 Dec <= +48, LoTSS DR2 = 27% of the north - a null must state which survey saw the position and at what rms); lesson 10 (template controls: AR Sco and ASKAP J1745-5051 must be recovered by branches A/B on the pipeline's own configuration; GLEAM-X J0704/ILT J1101 must be listed as known-unrecoverable so their absence is not scored as a pipeline null); lesson 7 (bulk over per-position loops for the 30k-object crossmatches); the not-dead TESS cached-EB asset for period confirmation; near-IR (VHS/2MASS) for the M-dwarf characterisation.
feasibility_notes: Catalogues are all anonymous (VizieR TAP confirmed today for VLASS E1, RACS-low/mid, LoTSS DR2, Gaia; CASDA for RACS-low2; NRAO/CADC for VLASS E2/E3; the XP-WDMS table must be checked for a public copy - if only in the journal, request it from the authors). Branches A/B are a few days of crossmatching plus ~50-100 vettings. Branch C needs ~30k image cutouts from the LoTSS and CASDA cutout services - throttled, no bulk-download guarantee; budget weeks and check rate limits before committing. Archive-only confirmation covers the optical period, the WD component (GALEX/XP) and the radio position/polarisation; the LPT pulse confirmation itself needs the radio pros (community-confirm). Gaia DR4 (Dec 2026) will add epoch astrometry and better WD+M binarity flags.
novelty_per_labor_guess: High per object, low yield: branches A/B cost days and most likely return 0-3 objects, but any confirmed radio-loud WD+M binary joins a class with fewer than ten members; branch C is the only route to the sporadic LPT hosts and is weeks of throttled image work with an unknown but non-zero yield.

title: Lane NIR-1: Pre-WISE-gap turn-ons and turn-offs — 2MASS (1997–2001) vs the three accidental UHS epochs (J 2012–17 / K 2017–24 / H 2019–24) and VHS, at |b|>5
what_we_would_find: Galactic objects whose near-IR state changed by >=1.5–2.5 mag between 2MASS (1997.5–2001.1) and ~2012 and then STAYED changed, so they are flat in every survey that can see variability (unTimely 2010–2020, VarWISE, Gaia DR3 2014–17, ZTF 2018+, PGIR 2018–22). Brightening direction: decade-long accretion outbursts (FU Ori-type; ~30–40 known in the Galaxy) that erupted 2001–2012 outside Spitzer-covered clouds, symbiotic slow novae (PU Vul / V1016 Cyg class, ~3 per half-century known), and dust-thinning brightenings of enshrouded AGB stars (the 'non-variable OH/IR brightening' phenomenon, arXiv:2008.06897, only ever measured in the plane). Fading direction: stars Ks<12.5 in 2000 that are >=2.5 mag fainter or absent in ALL three UHS epochs — dust-cocoon events (V605 Aql-type), multi-year total eclipses by dusty disks, and a near-IR analogue of VASCO 'vanished' sources, which has never been attempted in the infrared. Every survivor is an individually new-to-knowledge object, not a catalogue entry.
data_sources: 2MASS PSC 1997.5–2001.1 (10-sigma J 15.8 / H 15.1 / Ks 14.3; PSC extends to ~Ks 15.5 at lower quality; fields ph_qual, cc_flg, rd_flg, mp_flg (known-asteroid flag), prox, scan date) — held locally in WSA/VSA and at NOIRLab Data Lab (twomass.psc)

UHS DR3 at WSA (uhsSource / uhsDetection / uhsDetectionAll): J 2012-05-19 to 2017-01-31 (5-sigma 19.6 Vega), K 2017-07 to 2024-08 (18.0), H 2019-01 to 2024-07 (19.0); 0<dec<+60, ~12,700 deg^2 outside UKIDSS LAS/GPS/GCS; bands are SEPARATE campaigns, merged at 2 arcsec; uhsDetectionAll adds repeat/deprecated frames to 2024-08-01 (extra epochs); ppErrBits carry crosstalk/persistence/saturation flags

VHS DR6 at VSA (vhsSource / vhsDetection with per-detection MJD): 2009–2021, ~16,700 deg^2 south; YJ and HKs observed in separate concatenated OBs (J and Ks are NOT contemporaneous) so J-vs-Ks epoch separation must be read from vhsDetection.mjdObs; J ~20.2, Ks ~18.1 Vega 5-sigma (verify per tile)

WSA/VSA XNeighbour tables to the local 2MASS copies (10 arcsec default radius; confirm uhsSourceXtwomass_psc / vhsSourceXtwomass_psc names in the schema browser) — fallback: Data Lab q3c join of an uploaded UHS/VHS extract against twomass.psc
Gaia DR3 (PM propagation of every match to the 2MASS scan epoch; Gaia-absent sources searched at 10 arcsec)

PGIR DR1 at NOIRLab Data Lab (dec>-29, 2018-10 to ~2022-10, 1–3 night cadence, J<14.9 off-plane, >=100 epochs) — current NIR state for any candidate that has a 2MASS J<15.5 seed (2MASS-seeded, so absent-in-2MASS brighteners have no PGIR LC: a known blind spot, not a null)

unTimely (unWISE biannual coadd catalogues, 16 W1/W2 epochs 2010–2020, W1 to ~17.5–18 Vega, 6 arcsec pixels) — mid-IR state across the whole WISE era; used as a state check only (stand-alone NEOWISE variability is a closed lane)

SPHEREx QR2 (IRSA, weekly since Oct 2025; survey since ~May 2025 with two completed 6-month all-sky passes and a third under way; 0.75–5 um, 102 channels, 6.2 arcsec pixels; single-pass 5-sigma ~18.8–19.1 AB per channel at 0.75–3.8 um, i.e. K~17 Vega; per-target Tractor forced photometry via the IRSA Data Explorer; bulk via s3://nasa-irsa-spherex/qr with --no-sign-request) — a 2025–26 spectrum that classifies FUor (CO bandhead/H2O absorption) vs symbiotic/nova (emission lines) vs dusty AGB without a telescope

Multi-epoch NIR map for the record: many-epoch = VVV/VVVX+VIRAC2 (560 deg^2 bulge/plane, 50–300 Ks epochs 2010–2019, 545M stars; heavily team-mined), VMC (LMC/SMC, 12 Ks epochs; team-mined), VIDEO/UltraVISTA/UKIDSS UDS+DXS (<20 deg^2 extragalactic), PGIR DR1 (dec>-29 nightly J), SPHEREx (all-sky, 6-month passes); accidental two/three-epoch = UHS (J/K/H campaigns), VHS (YJ vs HKs OBs), UKIDSS LAS (YJ vs HK visits), 2MASS vs any of them (10–25 yr, K<14.3); Euclid Q1 (63 deg^2, Y/J/H to 24.5 AB, public) now and DR1-Foundation ~1,900 deg^2 in Nov 2026
selection: BRIGHTENING channel (blend-immune: a 2MASS blend can only make 2MASS BRIGHTER than either resolved UHS component): UHS K (or VHS Ks) in 11.0–13.5 (above the WFCAM/VIRCAM saturation, >=15-sigma if it had existed in 2MASS), mergedClass -1/-2, ppErrBits clean, |b|>5, |beta|>15 or SkyBoT-clean at the UHS epoch, not in 2MASS XSC; require EITHER no 2MASS PSC source within 3 arcsec after Gaia-PM propagation and 2MASS local coverage proven (cc_flg of neighbours = 000, no K<6 star within 30 arcsec) OR a measured 2MASS Ks fainter by >=1.5 mag; then demand the two OTHER UHS bands (J 2012–17 and H 2019–24) also sit >=1.5 mag above 2MASS J/H — three independent epochs agreeing means a persistent state and kills Miras, whose random-phase epochs disagree. Volume: ~15M UHS K<13.5 sources -> ~0.1–0.3% without a 2MASS match (~15k–45k) -> after crosstalk/confusion/galaxy flags ~500–2,000 for cutout vetting (WSA/VSA JHK cutouts + 2MASS Atlas cutouts, kept under IRSA's ~1,100-query session budget or pulled from the 2MASS image archive) -> 10–50 real persistent brighteners, 5–30 uncatalogued. FADING channel: 2MASS Ks<12.5, ph_qual AAA, cc_flg 000, mp_flg 0, prox>10 arcsec, |b|>5, with UHS K AND J AND H each >=2.5 mag fainter or absent, no UHS neighbour brighter than K=15 within 5 arcsec, Gaia PM<100 mas/yr or no Gaia, SkyBoT run at the 2MASS scan date; ~8M input -> <100 survivors -> 5–20 genuine. South: identical logic with VHS J/Ks per-band MJDs and DES/DECaPS for the optical state. Expected total: 15–70 new-to-knowledge objects, of which 0–3 FUor-class, 0–2 slow symbiotic novae, 5–20 'vanished/cocooned' stars.
main_false_positive_channel: WFCAM/VIRCAM crosstalk and persistence ghosts of bright stars (appear as point sources at fixed pixel offsets; ppErrBits catch most, cutouts catch the rest) and 2MASS confusion-masking near bright stars (brightening channel); asteroids and 2MASS artefacts at the 2MASS epoch, plus blends, for the fading channel (2MASS blends are brighter, so a 'fade' can be a resolved pair — the 5 arcsec isolation cut and the 3-epoch requirement handle it); high-proper-motion stars (>130 mas/yr moves 2 arcsec in 15 yr — Gaia propagation); Miras caught at two of three UHS epochs near maximum (residual; check PGIR/ZTF periodicity).
credit_channel: VSX (named credit) for every confirmed variable: FUOR/EXOR/YSO, ZAND/symbiotic nova, RCB-like or UNIQUE for vanished sources; AstroNote for any object whose SPHEREx 2025–26 spectrum shows the event is ongoing; community-confirm: FUor/eruptive-YSO candidates go to Contreras Peña / Lucas / Hillenbrand (they actively follow up such candidates spectroscopically), symbiotic candidates to Munari / Merc / the SALT symbiotic identification programme (arXiv:2512.01744). No propagation component: each object is discovered, not re-filed.
why_not_already_done: The only groups that have ever compared 2MASS with a later deep NIR epoch for variability are Contreras Peña & Lucas (Extreme IR variables from UKIDSS I/II, 2014/2017: 618 dK>1 stars) and the VVV team — both strictly in the Galactic plane (|b|<5, GPS and VVV footprints), because their science is YSOs in the plane. UHS K and H did not exist until June 2023 / Sept 2025, and the UHS team (Dye, Bruursema, Lawrence, Schneider) publishes brown dwarfs, high-proper-motion objects (arXiv:2509.22605) and quasars, not variability. The VHS team (McMahon, Banerji) used 2MASS-vs-VHS differences for quasar ensemble variability only (arXiv:2504.16733), proving the method and ignoring stars. VASCO (Villarroel) hunts vanished sources only in POSS-to-Pan-STARRS/Gaia optical. Every NEOWISE-era catalogue (unTimely variables arXiv:2511.22071 with 8.3M W1 variables; VarWISE arXiv:2605.19059; the ISO/Spitzer/WISE 27-year YSO study arXiv:2601.21013 — 39 large-amplitude YSOs, explicitly limited to Spitzer-identified YSOs) can only see changes inside 2010–2024, and PGIR/Gaia/ZTF only inside 2014–2026: anything that changed between 2001 and ~2012 and stayed is flat in all of them. Honest caveats: (i) within Spitzer-covered clouds the YSO-eruption subset is partially mined by arXiv:2601.21013, so our residual there is non-YSO classes and the fading direction; (ii) the UHS K/H campaigns are recent enough that a UHS-team variability paper could appear at any time — the window is now.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 3 generalised: 'constant-bright new sources are structurally invisible to every broker' becomes 'constant-CHANGED sources are invisible to every within-window variability catalogue' — we select on a 25-year static offset, not on variability. Lesson 9: 2MASS coverage/cc_flg and UHS ppErrBits are checked BEFORE any absence claim. Lesson 10: the pipeline must recover, on its own configuration, known FUors in the footprint (HBC 722 = V2493 Cyg, erupted 2010, dec +44), a known long-decline RCB and a known vanished-source case before any null is reported. Lesson 5: VHS/UHS J/K as physical anchors. Lesson 7: all bulk work in WSA/VSA SQL and Data Lab TAP; IRSA only for <1,000 cutouts and SPHEREx per-target photometry. Lesson 8/unTimely: free mid-IR state across 2010–2020.
feasibility_notes: No new accounts: WSA/VSA freeform SQL is public for UHS/VHS, Data Lab TAP is anonymous, SPHEREx QR2 is public with no proprietary period. Extractions of ~25M rows are done in dec strips under the WSA 30-min query cap; compute is laptop-scale (cross-match + flags in minutes). IRSA per-position use stays under the ~1,100-query limit (cutouts for the vetted shortlist only). Archive-only confirmation IS possible for the brightening channel: three UHS epochs + PGIR/unTimely flatness + a SPHEREx 0.75–5 um spectrum (CO/H2O absorption vs emission lines vs hot-dust continuum) classify without a telescope; a professional spectrum is a bonus, not a gate. For vanished sources the archive can prove the fade and the dust (unTimely/LS-DR10 forced WISE) but not the physics; those go out as AstroNotes for the community. Time to first vetted list: ~2 weeks, dominated by cutout inspection of ~1,000 candidates.
novelty_per_labor_guess: HIGH for the top handful (a new FUor or slow symbiotic nova is a headline object; each infrared 'vanished' star is individually publishable), MEDIUM for the bulk (uncatalogued AGB dust-thinning brighteners). Rough odds: >=1 genuinely new eruptive/vanished object ~50–70%; >=1 FUor-class object ~20–30%; total new VSX-grade objects 15–70 for ~2 weeks of mostly image-vetting labour.

title: Lane NIR-2: The PGIR 'excluded middle' — short-lived and 0.5–2 mag J-band events on optically-dark 2MASS stars at |b|>5 (nightly cadence, 2018–2022)
what_we_would_find: A census that does not exist: days-to-months near-IR events of 0.5–2 mag on stars that are invisible or extremely red in the optical, outside the Galactic plane. Concretely: obscured symbiotic outbursts (Z And-type, 0.5–1.5 mag J rises over 30–300 d) on IR-only giants (predicted Galactic symbiotic population 10^3–10^5 vs ~300 known; the obscured tail is where a J-band survey beats ZTF); embedded-YSO accretion bursts and dust dips in Taurus, Perseus, Ophiuchus, Orion, lambda Ori, Mon R2 and Cepheus (all at dec>-29) that NEOWISE cannot resolve in time (6-month cadence) or space (6 arcsec pixels); RCB/DY Per 'mini-declines' whose optical counterpart fell into a ZTF detection gap; and unexplained IR-only flares or dips on Gaia-invisible stars. The PGIR team's own census (128 spectroscopically classified stars, 92% at |b|<15) selected only >=2 mag, smooth, persistent variables — the 0.5–2 mag and short-event domain at high latitude has never been read.
data_sources: pgir_dr1 at NOIRLab Astro Data Lab (TAP https://datalab.noirlab.edu/tap): sources (148,840,740 rows: pts_key, tmcjmag, tmchmag, meanmag, minmag, maxmag, rmsmag, psfcontam, glat/glon, elat/elon), photometry (47,590,715,733 rows: obsjd, magpsf, magpsferr, magpsflim, flags, stackquadid), exposures (4,133,007 rows: limmag, saturmag, zp, airmass); dec>-29, ~15,000–18,000 deg^2, Oct 2018 to ~Oct 2022, 1–3 night cadence, >=100 epochs off-plane and >=500 in the northern plane, J<14.9 off-plane / <13.0 in-plane, saturation J~8.5 (pre-2020) then ~6.0, resampled pixel 4.35 arcsec; forced photometry at 2MASS J<15.5 positions (2MASS-seeded)
Data Lab twomass.psc, gaia_dr3.gaia_source, allwise/unwise tables for server-side joins (no per-position rate limit)

ZTF DR light curves for the optical state during each J event (IRSA per-position within the ~1,100-query budget for the shortlist; bulk via the documented HATS/S3 endpoint if the shortlist grows) — detection gaps read as faint states per session lesson 1
UHS J/H/K (2012–2024) and VHS J/Ks as independent epoch anchors bracketing the PGIR window; 2MASS as the 2000 anchor
unTimely W1/W2 (16 epochs 2010–2020) for the contemporaneous mid-IR state of 2018–2020 events (state check only)
SPHEREx QR2 2025–26 per-target spectrophotometry (emission lines = symbiotic/nova; CO absorption = YSO/AGB; dust bump) for current state and class
Novelty gate catalogues: VSX, SIMBAD, Gaia DR3 vari_classifier and LPV tables, SPICY and Marton+ WISE YSO candidates, Akras/Merc symbiotic candidate lists, Tisserand 2020 WISE-RCB candidates
selection: Footprint dec>-29, |b|>5 (plane bycatch optional at J<13). Seed: 2MASS J<14.5 (>=0.4 mag above the off-plane limit so a 0.5-mag dip stays detected), optically dark by any of: no Gaia DR3 source within 1.5 arcsec, or G-J>6, or tmcjmag-tmchmag>0.6 with G-J>4. Cleanliness: psfcontam=0 (no other 2MASS source inside the ~10 arcsec PGIR PSF aperture), 2MASS prox>10 arcsec, flags F2–F6 clean, >=100 epochs. First cut in ONE SQL on the sources table: 0.5<=(maxmag-minmag)<2.0 (strictly below the LAV census's >=2 mag cut) with rmsmag<0.15 (event on a flat baseline), OR (maxmag-meanmag)>0.5 (dip) OR (meanmag-minmag)>0.5 (flare). Then pull photometry for the shortlist and require >=3 consecutive epochs deviating by >5x magpsferr and brighter than magpsflim, event duration 3–300 d, von Neumann eta>0.2 or non-periodic (periodic ~1-yr smooth variables = Miras, rejected). Volume: ~45M 2MASS J<14.5 in footprint -> optically-dark cut ~1–3x10^5 -> variability first cut ~5–10x10^3 -> contamination/flag-clean ~1–2x10^3 -> LC + cutout vetting -> 50–150 real events -> 30–100 uncatalogued after the novelty gate. Expect roughly: 10–40 embedded-YSO events, 5–20 dusty-AGB/RCB-like dips, 2–10 symbiotic-outburst candidates, a few unexplained.
main_false_positive_channel: Blending in PGIR's ~10 arcsec effective aperture (a variable neighbour leaks into the forced photometry of a constant star) — killed by psfcontam=0 plus 2MASS prox and by checking that the 2MASS seed is the brightest object in the aperture; single-night outliers from bad zero-point/airmass nights (F4/F5), moving objects crossing the aperture at |beta|<10 (one-night 'flares' — the >=3-consecutive-night rule removes them), saturation at J<8.5 pre-2020, and Mira phase coverage (0.5–2 mag smooth ~1-yr variations) which is a class rejection, not an artefact.
credit_channel: VSX (named credit) for each new symbiotic/YSO/dusty variable; AstroNote for any event still active in SPHEREx 2025–26 data; community-confirm: symbiotic candidates to the SALT symbiotic identification programme (arXiv:2512.01744) and Munari/Merc, YSO events to Hillenbrand/Contreras Peña, RCB-like dips to Karambelkar/Tisserand. All discovery, no propagation.
why_not_already_done: The PGIR team (De, Kasliwal, Karambelkar; PASP 2025, arXiv:2510.18959) built their census with peak-to-peak >=2 mag, >50 epochs, median SNR>10 and von Neumann ratio <=0.2 — i.e. smooth, persistent, large-amplitude stars suitable for spectroscopic follow-up; 0.5–2 mag events and short erratic events are excluded by construction, and 92% of what they found is within |b|<15. Their real-time pipeline finds NEW transients by difference imaging (obscured novae, De+2021), not modulations of already-catalogued stars. DR1 has been public at Data Lab since Oct 2024 with no external variability census found in searches — the 47.6-billion-row photometry table is intimidating, and the near-IR time-domain community is tiny (Caltech PGIR/WINTER, a few YSO groups) and busy with its own instruments. Honest risks: the PGIR team could run a lower-amplitude census next (the window is now); symbiotic yields at |b|>5 may be <=5; DR1 is 2MASS-seeded, so anything born after 2001 is absent (a stated blind spot).
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 6 turned into a selection: MAD/rms statistics barely move for a rare event, so we cut on min/max excursions and consecutive-epoch runs, not on rms. Lesson 4: per-frame magpsflim is the honest detection reference; the slope of magpsf vs magpsflim (~0 for real sources, ~1 for threshold artefacts) is applied to every candidate. Lesson 1: ZTF detection gaps give the optical state during the J event (optical-vs-IR disagreement). Lesson 7: all joins on Data Lab TAP, IRSA only for the shortlist. Lesson 2: the DR1 seeding blind spot is declared, not silently converted into a null. Lesson 10: recover the census's own published LAVs (e.g. their 8 symbiotics and 16 RCBs) on our pipeline before any absence claim.
feasibility_notes: Anonymous Data Lab TAP; first cut is one async SQL on the 149M-row sources table (minutes), photometry pulls for <=10^4 pts_key are routine; laptop compute. IRSA usage limited to ZTF LCs and SPHEREx forced photometry for a few hundred objects (under the ~1,100 limit). Archive-only confirmation is real: PGIR LC + UHS/VHS epochs + unTimely mid-IR state + SPHEREx 0.75–5 um spectrum classify symbiotic vs YSO vs dusty AGB; VSX filing needs no telescope. ~1–2 weeks to a filed first batch.
novelty_per_labor_guess: MEDIUM-HIGH in count (tens of uncatalogued IR variables from ~1–2 weeks of work), MEDIUM in class (mostly symbiotic/YSO/AGB physics) with a genuine tail of unexplained IR-only events. Rough odds: >=10 new VSX-grade objects ~70%; >=1 obscured symbiotic outburst ~40%; >=1 physically novel IR-only event ~25%.

title: Lane NIR-3: Optical-off / infrared-on — 2MASS (2000) vs Gaia DR3 mean-G (2014.5–2017.4) optical-deficit selection for stars in multi-year dust declines and long eclipses
what_we_would_find: Stars that were normal-coloured and optically bright in 1998–2001 but were >=2.5 mag (or >=4 mag if Gaia-absent) too faint in G during the ENTIRE Gaia DR3 window relative to what their 2MASS J-Ks colour allows along the extinction vector — i.e. objects in a decline that started before 2012 and had not recovered by 2018, which are 'constant-faint' and therefore unclassifiable by every light-curve survey (Gaia DR3 classifier, ASAS-SN, ZTF, PGIR). Classes: R CrB and DY Per stars in multi-year declines (only ~160 Galactic RCBs known against predictions of several hundred; the pre-2012 long-decline subset is untouched by all existing discovery channels), epsilon Aur / KH 15D-type long total eclipses by dusty disks, dust-cocoon events on post-AGB and yellow supergiants, and an unexplained residue of optically vanished, infrared-persistent stars. The near-IR half of the test — UHS/VHS K (2012–2024) unchanged while the optical is off — is what separates dust obscuration (K persists via warm-dust emission) from grey/vanished cases.
data_sources: Gaia archive ADQL: gaiadr3.gaia_source (phot_g_mean_mag, phot_g_n_obs, ipd_frac_multi_peak, pm, ruwe) joined to gaiadr3.tmass_psc_xsc_best_neighbour (Gaia's own proper-motion-propagated match to 2MASS) plus gaiadr3.vari_summary / vari_classifier_result (153 DR3 RCB classifications = control set); mean epoch 2014.5–2017.4
2MASS PSC (ph_qual, cc_flg, mp_flg, prox, scan date, XSC exclusion) — locally in WSA/VSA and Data Lab
UHS DR3 (K 2017–24, J 2012–17, H 2019–24) and VHS DR6 (J, Ks from separate OBs, 2009–2021): the infrared state anchor across the whole decline window
PGIR DR1 (nightly J 2018–2022, dec>-29): recoveries and mini-declines
ZTF DR (2018–2026 r/g): current optical state read from detection gaps and recoveries (per-position for the <=500 shortlist)
unTimely W1/W2 (2010–2020): dust formation appears as a mid-IR RISE anti-correlated with the optical fade — the RCB fingerprint; LS DR10 forced unWISE (W1>19.3 Vega limits) for the south
SPHEREx QR2 2025–26: hot-dust bump at 2–5 um and C2/CN bands classify RCB/HdC vs eclipsing vs cocoon without a telescope

Novelty gate: Tisserand 2020 WISE-RCB candidate list, Gaia DR3 RCB class, ASAS-SN RCB search (Shields+2019), Karambelkar+2021/2024 ZTF+PGIR RCB lists, VSX, SIMBAD; SkyBoT/Horizons (existing project tooling) at the 2MASS scan epoch
Gaia DR4 (2 Dec 2026): epoch photometry 2014–2020 for every candidate will show whether the deficit is a smooth decline — a free upgrade in 10 weeks
selection: 2MASS J<13.5, ph_qual=AAA, cc_flg=000, mp_flg=0, prox>6 arcsec, not in XSC, |b|>5, outside globular/open-cluster cores, 0.2<J-Ks<1.1 (excludes Miras and dust-enshrouded AGB and deeply embedded YSOs; keeps RCB-at-maximum J-Ks 0.4–1.0, F–K giants/supergiants and eclipsing systems). Gaia test, either: (a) no Gaia DR3 source with G<20 within 2 arcsec after PM propagation (optical deficit >=4 mag at J<13.5), or (b) G-J > 2.9 + 3.4*(J-Ks-0.2) + 2.5, i.e. 2.5 mag redder than the reddest static star along the extinction vector (A_G:A_J:A_Ks ~ 0.85:0.28:0.11 gives slope E(G-J)/E(J-Ks) ~ 3.4; the M-giant end of the locus has (G-J)_0 ~ 2.9). Exclude anything within 60 arcsec of a G<5 star or with ipd_frac_multi_peak>10. Infrared test: UHS/VHS K within 1 mag of 2MASS Ks = 'IR-on' (dust obscuration class); K also >=2 mag down = grey/vanished class. Volume: ~20M 2MASS stars pass the colour/quality cuts -> ~2–5x10^3 raw deficit sources -> asteroid (SkyBoT at 2MASS epoch), artefact and blend cleaning -> 200–500 -> classified: ~30–60 known RCBs in decline, ~10 known long-eclipse/UXor systems, 5–25 new RCB/DY Per candidates, 1–10 new long-eclipse or dust-cocoon systems, plus an unexplained residue. Controls: R CrB itself (2007–2018 decline overlaps DR3), known long-decline RCBs, a known epsilon-Aur-type system, must all be recovered before any null.
main_false_positive_channel: Asteroids at the 2MASS epoch (solar J-Ks~0.4 sits inside the colour window; dominates at |beta|<15 — SkyBoT per candidate with the PSC scan date, mp_flg only covers asteroids known in 2003); Gaia crowding incompleteness and bright-star wings (mitigated by |b|>5, cluster and 60 arcsec-of-G<5 exclusions); 2MASS blends (bounded at 0.75 mag for equal pairs, so the 2.5-mag threshold is immune); very-high-PM stars (Gaia's PM-propagated crossmatch handles them; re-search at 10 arcsec); 2MASS artefacts (cc_flg); Miras in bright phase with J-Ks 1.0–1.1 (gated by Gaia LPV/ASAS-SN/ZTF periodicity). Eclipsing binaries with total eclipses lasting >=3 yr are findings, not false positives.
credit_channel: VSX (named credit) as RCB:, DYPER:, EA with multi-year eclipse, or UNIQUE; RCB candidates go to Tisserand / Clayton / Karambelkar for H-deficiency spectroscopy (community-confirm; these groups actively solicit candidates and name the finder); AstroNote for any object currently recovering in ZTF/PGIR/SPHEREx.
why_not_already_done: Every RCB discovery channel needs the decline or recovery to happen INSIDE its own window: Tisserand 2020 selects on WISE colours of warm dust (and Karambelkar+2024 showed 2 of 75 light-curve-selected PGIR candidates were missed by that colour cut), ASAS-SN (Shields+2019) needs declines seen 2012–2018 at V<17, Karambelkar+2021/2024 need ZTF/PGIR declines, and the Gaia DR3 classifier (153 RCBs) needs variability within 2014–2017. A star already deep in decline before 2012 and still faint after 2018 is constant-faint everywhere — the mirror of session lesson 3. Tisserand+2022 used 2MASS+Gaia to find dustless HdC stars, but as a static colour locus, not as a 15-year epoch difference. VASCO's vanished-source work is optical-only. Two targeted searches found no published '2MASS-bright / Gaia-faint' epoch-disagreement catalogue (verify on ADS before starting). Honest risks: the RCB field is crowded and fast; the unique pre-2012 long-decline pool is bounded (perhaps 5–25 objects Galaxy-wide); the unexplained residue may be where the real novelty sits. This is NOT the closed bimodal state-cycler lane: it is a single 15-year epoch difference between two static all-sky catalogues, no ZTF cycling, and the targets are single events, not cyclers.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 3 (constant-state objects are invisible to light-curve classifiers) applied in the fading direction; lesson 1 (ZTF detection gaps and recoveries give the 2018–2026 optical state without downloading bulk light curves); lesson 5 (UHS/VHS K as the infrared persistence anchor); lesson 8 (LS DR10 forced unWISE for deep southern W1 limits); lesson 9 (prove Gaia and 2MASS coverage — bright-star masks, crowding — before any 'absent' claim); lesson 10 (R CrB and known long-eclipse systems recovered on the pipeline's own configuration first); the project's existing SkyBoT/Horizons tooling closes the asteroid channel.
feasibility_notes: One ADQL job on the Gaia archive (or Data Lab), no new accounts; ~10^3-scale vetting; IRSA stays under the rate limit (ZTF per-position only for the <=500 shortlist; SPHEREx Data Explorer per target). Archive-only confirmation is genuine: unTimely mid-IR rise + UHS/VHS K persistence + PGIR/ZTF recovery + SPHEREx dust spectrum make a self-contained decline-by-dust case; the hydrogen-deficiency proof needs a professional spectrum (community-confirm). Gaia DR4 epoch photometry (2 Dec 2026) will retro-test every candidate for free. ~1 week to a filed first batch.
novelty_per_labor_guess: MEDIUM-HIGH: a rare class (5–25 new RCB/DY Per candidates plausible against ~160 known) plus 1–10 long-eclipse/cocoon systems for roughly one week of labour, but with intense professional competition and a bounded pool; the unexplained 'optically vanished, infrared-persistent' residue is the upside. Rough odds: >=1 new RCB-class candidate ~60%; >=1 new long-eclipse/cocoon system ~40%; >=1 object with no standard explanation ~20%.

title: Faint recurrent eruptors in the DES-SN/HELM legacy fields: mine the public DES-SN5YR DiffImg candidate list for stellar-coincident outbursters (period-bouncer / AM CVn / faint-quiescence dwarf novae at r_q = 21-24.5), then confirm recurrence with HELM DR1 (2019-22) and NSC per-exposure quiescence (2013-19)
what_we_would_find: Dwarf novae whose quiescent counterpart is r = 21-24.5 (below ZTF, Gaia, ATLAS, ASAS-SN in quiescence AND mostly at dec < -27 where ZTF never looks), caught in 1-10 outbursts over 2013-2018 by DES-SN's 7-day cadence and again in 2019-2022 by HELM. Physically: high-latitude CVs at 1.5-5 kpc, the population where WZ Sge-type / post-period-minimum ('period bouncer') systems dominate; each object gets a multi-outburst, multi-band (griz) light curve, an amplitude (4-8 mag), a recurrence time and a quiescent colour. Exotic bycatch with expected count <0.5 but nonzero: a faint quiescent LMXB/UCXB outburst in the CDF-S (Chandra deep) or XMM-LSS deep X-ray fields, or an AM CVn outburster (P_orb 20-45 min). Concrete expected count: CV column density at |b| = 45-65 deg is 0.2-0.6 per deg^2 (rho_0 = 4.8e-6 pc^-3, scale height 300-450 pc), so 5-16 CVs along the 27 deg^2 of DES-SN, ~70% with r_q > 21, ~55% dwarf-nova type, ~70% outbursting at least once in 5 yr => 2-5 new DNe from DES-SN, +1-2 from HELM's extra COSMOS/S-CVZ 11 deg^2 => 3-7 new-to-knowledge objects, each VSX-fileable as UG/UGWZ: with a real recurrence record.
data_sources: DES-SN5YR public release: 31,636 DiffImg light curves (all 5 seasons, griz, forced photometry after trigger), github.com/des-science/DES-SN5YR + Zenodo + ReadTheDocs (Sanchez et al. 2024): 75% are not SNe; 13,507 pass a multi-season cut, so ~18,000 multi-season objects (AGN + variable stars + artefacts) are in the file and never classified

HELM DR1 (Zhang et al. 2024, ApJS 274, 42): 2019A-2022A, 3-6 d cadence, 2 back-to-back exposures per filter per epoch, exposure 160/140/180 s in g/r/i, single-exposure 5-sigma r ~ 22.9-23.5, 5.4M sources with >=3 detections, PSF+AUTO mags; open HTTP directory https://ariel.astro.illinois.edu/helm/ with lightcurves_<FIELD>/ per field (CDF-S, XMM-LSS, ELAIS-S1, Stripe-82, COSMOS, S-CVZ) + median_source_catalogs/ (no account; read the Data Release Note first). HELM has NO forced photometry / upper limits: a source that fades below ~23 simply has no row (lesson 1 applies)

NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2 via anonymous Data Lab TAP (verified today): nsc_dr2.meas (measid, objectid, exposure, ccdnum, filter, mjd, x, y, ra, dec, mag_auto, mag_aper1/2/4/8, fwhm, class_star, flags), nsc_dr2.exposure (mjd, dateobs, exptime, fwhm, zpterm, zptermsig, depth95, depth10sig), nsc_dr2.chip (vertex_ra1-4/vertex_dec1-4 CCD footprints). DECam coverage 2012-09-23 to 2019-11-16, 340,952 exposures. Verified: C3 box has 817 r / 1,156 g / 1,063 i / 1,870 z exposures over 373 r-nights; one r = 20.06 star (id 144203_393215) has 831 dated r rows spanning MJD 56234-58801 with 184/386 nights carrying >=2 r exposures

DES Y3 deep-field coadd catalogue (Hartley et al. 2022, r ~ 26-27) or DES DR2 coadd + HELM median catalogue for the persistent counterpart and morphology (EXTENDED_CLASS_COADD / class_star); LS DR10 forced unWISE W1/W2 (AGN kill, lesson 8); NSC object proper motions

DECam DDF alerts/light curves (Graham et al. 2023, 2024: 4,413 + 2,020 DIA light curves; ANTARES loci; 3-d cadence 2021A-2023A) for the ELAIS-S1 (E1/E2) overlap only; Stripe 82 known-CV lists (SDSS) as pipeline controls in S1/S2
selection: Sky: the 10 DES-SN pointings (27 deg^2; C1-3, X1-3, E1-2, S1-2; |b| = 45-65 deg) plus HELM's COSMOS (3 pointings) and S-CVZ (1) for the 2019-22 leg (38 deg^2 total). Step 1 (hours): take all 31,636 DiffImg candidates; keep those within 0.5 arcsec of a point-like coadd source (class_star > 0.8 or EXTENDED_CLASS_COADD <= 1) with coadd r = 21-24.5, and with per-epoch DiffImg flux showing >= 1 episode of amplitude >= 2.5 mag above the coadd magnitude, rise <= 3 d, duration 5-40 d, g-r <= 0.3 near peak; require detections in >= 2 exposures on >= 2 nights per episode (DES-SN's own trigger already guarantees 2 nights). Step 2: AGN kill: LS DR10 W1-W2 < 0.5 or W1 non-detection (a r ~ 23 CV has W1 > 20; a r ~ 23 AGN is W1 ~ 18-19.5), NSC proper motion > 3 sigma if available, no extended host within 1 arcsec. Step 3: pull NSC meas rows (2013-2019) for the survivors to get quiescent level and same-night multi-exposure confirmation of every outburst point; Step 4: HELM DR1 light curve 2019-2022 for recurrence (gaps in HELM rows = quiescence below ~23). Step 5: DDF/ANTARES 2021-23 for E1/E2 objects. Expected funnel: 31,636 -> ~18,000 multi-season -> ~3,000 with point-like counterpart -> ~50-200 outburst-shaped -> 3-7 CV-classified after AGN/artefact kill; controls: recover the SDSS Stripe 82 known dwarf novae inside S1/S2 and any VSX CVs in the other fields BEFORE any absence claim (lesson 10).
main_false_positive_channel: (1) AGN on compact/unresolved hosts (thousands in the multi-season set; killed by WISE colour, zero PM, stochastic rather than outburst-shaped light curves, and multi-year drifts); (2) SNe on point-like faint hosts (single episode, 30-100 d, red late colours, offset >= 0.2 arcsec from the host centroid at NSC's 0.05-0.1 arcsec precision; require >= 2 episodes or a WZ-type profile to beat this); (3) M-dwarf flares (single-night, so already excluded by the 2-night trigger, but multi-night flares can leak: require duration >= 5 d); (4) DiffImg artefacts near bright stars (autoscan passed them at ~30%; kill by requiring the same-night NSC meas rows to show the brightening in >= 2 exposures); (5) RR Lyrae/EBs misread as outbursts (periodic; amplitude < 1.3 mag).
credit_channel: VSX (named credit; UG/UGWZ:/UGSU: with the DES+HELM multi-outburst light curve as evidence); AstroNote/TNS only if the exotic bycatch (LMXB-like or AM CVn) appears; a population note (RNAAS/co-authored with a CV person, per publication policy) if >= 5 objects.
why_not_already_done: The people who touched these exact photons: (a) DES-SN (Kessler, Sanchez, Wiseman, Moller) built DiffImg for SN cosmology; the 2024 release paper states 75% of DiffImg candidates are not SNe and that AGN/variable stars were removed by a multi-season cut, i.e. the Galactic eruptors were deliberately thrown out, never catalogued; Pursiainen's fast-transient work was extragalactic. (b) HELM (Shen, Zhang, Liu, Martini) is an AGN reverberation program; their DR1 paper demonstrates RR Lyrae light curves but performs no Galactic census, and notes itself that sources without a static counterpart are missed. (c) The DECam DDF team (Graham, Aldoroty) did stellar flares/variables in their Galactic fields and DIA candidates in COSMOS/ELAIS (2,020 light curves) - they may hold a few E1/E2 dwarf novae unlabelled; check their classification table first. (d) CV specialists (Inight/Gansicke: Gaia+SDSS; Pala: 150 pc; Kato/vsnet: ZTF/ASAS-SN) work at r < 20.5 and largely dec > -30; none has a product at r_q = 21-24 with 5-yr weekly cadence. I found no ADS/arXiv paper mining DES-SN5YR DiffImg candidates or HELM DR1 for cataclysmic variables (searched 2026-09-19); the gate before starting is an ADS citation check of Sanchez+2024 and Zhang+2024.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 1 (censored light curves): HELM has no forced photometry, so missing HELM rows are the quiescent-state measurement, not missing data - the outburst amplitude comes from rows-vs-gaps. Lesson 6 (nsc_dr2.meas dated per-exposure rows; DES-SN deep fields give 3-5 same-night r exposures) makes every outburst point reproducible same-night (lesson 10's 'never ndet=1'). Lesson 8: LS DR10 forced unWISE is the free AGN discriminator at r ~ 23. Lesson 9: prove DDF/HELM pointing footprints actually cover each E1/E2 object before citing a DDF non-recurrence. Lesson 11: VSX credit; lesson 12 checked: Rubin DP1/DP2 are data-rights-only (US/Chile/in-kind) so the Rubin DDF recurrence leg is NOT available to this user - only DES/HELM/DDF are.
feasibility_notes: Access: DES-SN5YR = one GitHub/Zenodo download, no account; HELM = open HTTP directory, no account (read the Data Release Note for file format - per-field directories exist; bulk size unknown, likely GB-scale); NSC DR2 = anonymous Data Lab sync TAP verified today for schema, exposure, object and meas queries (a single-object meas query returned 831 rows promptly); rate limits/row caps for anonymous sync are unmeasured - pilot on 100 objects, checkpoint every batch, and shape-check outputs. Compute: trivial (10^4-10^5 light curves; laptop). Archive-only confirmation: YES - a multi-outburst light curve + point-like blue counterpart + WISE non-detection is VSX-grade for UG type; the UGWZ/period-bouncer sub-label stays a candidate (superhump periods need minute cadence). Labor: 1-2 days to first candidates; the whole lane is a week. Kill rule satisfied: bottleneck is vetting labor, not telescope time. Clock: none hard, but Rubin DDF alerts (if the public stream resumes) will eventually flag the 2025+ outbursts of the same objects.
novelty_per_labor_guess: HIGH per unit labor, LOW absolute yield: 3-7 genuinely new faint dwarf novae (candidate period bouncers) for ~1 week of work, because the hard part (5-yr difference imaging at r ~ 23.5) was done by DES and released. Per-object novelty moderate-high: nobody has recurrence-confirmed CVs at r_q > 22 in these fields.

title: Southern deep-eclipse census from DES wide-survey back-to-back filter pairs: point sources at r = 20-21.5 that vanish by >= 1.2 mag in two exposures taken 2.0 min apart (eclipsing WD+dM, double-WD and WD+BD binaries at 0.3-1.2 kpc below dec -30, where no time-domain survey below r ~ 19.5 has ever operated)
what_we_would_find: Eclipsing post-common-envelope white-dwarf binaries (WD+dM dominated in r, total eclipses of 4-15 min for P = 2-10 h) in the DES wide footprint (5,000 deg^2, dec -30 to -65 plus Stripe 82), quiescent r = 20-21.5, i.e. 0.5-1.2 kpc, thick-disc heights. Expected count (assumptions explicit): WD surface density at r 20-21.5 and |b| ~ 50 deg ~ 10-25 per deg^2 (Gaia EDR3 WD catalogue gives ~9-12 per deg^2 at G < 20.5 and growth flattens at 1-1.6 scale heights); close PCEB (P < 1 d) fraction 2-3%; eclipsing fraction ~10%; r-band depth > 1.2 mag in ~40% (WD-dominated) => 0.01-0.03 per deg^2 => 50-150 systems in the footprint; with ~45 exposures per object (measured mean ndet = 47, ndetr = 9.7) and eclipse duty 2-4%, P(>= 1 in-eclipse exposure) = 60-85%, and both exposures of a 2-min pair inside the eclipse in 50-70% of those => 20-90 pair-corroborated new eclipsing WD+dM candidates, versus ~130-170 eclipsing WDMS known in total (Parsons+2015: 71; ZTF +43 in 2023; the 2025 Gaia DR3 magnitude-limited WDMS catalogue finds 67 eclipsers, explicitly only from ZTF/CRTS at dec > -31). Rarer bycatch with expected 0-3: eclipsing double WDs and WD+brown-dwarf systems (deeper, shorter eclipses). Positive-sign twin from the same pipeline: faint dwarf novae caught in outburst in a 2-min pair (10-100 recurrence-corroborated over the footprint).
data_sources: nsc_dr2.object (per-band rrms/grms/irms/zrms, ndet, ndetr, class_star, pmra/pmdec) as pre-filter; measured in a 1 deg^2 DES box at (30,-45): 934 point sources at r 20-21.5 with >= 6 r detections, of which 2.1% have any-band rms > 0.3 mag

nsc_dr2.meas (mag_auto AND mag_aper2, flags, x, y, ccdnum, fwhm, per-row ra/dec) for the pre-filtered ~150-250k objects; nsc_dr2.exposure (mjd, filter, exptime, fwhm, zptermsig, depth95 ~ 23.9-24.1 for 90-s exposures, so a 2.5-mag eclipse of an r = 21 star is still a measured point, not a missing row); nsc_dr2.chip vertices for edge distance

Verified today from nsc_dr2.exposure: DES wide visits are back-to-back filter pairs at the same pointing 2.0 min apart (g->r, r->g, r->i, r->z, i->r all observed in the test box); pointings revisited 3-6 times in 85-95 s exposures across Y1-Y6 (DES ended Jan 2019; NSC DR2 runs to Nov 2019 so all DES wide data are in)

Counterpart physics without a telescope: Gaia DR3 (parallax/BP-RP for the ~30% with G < 21), GALEX NUV (WD excess; prove tile coverage per object, lesson 9), VHS J/Ks (dec < 0, J ~ 20.5 limit: the M dwarf at 0.5-1 kpc is J 16.5-20 - lesson 5), LS DR10 g-r/r-z composite colours and Tractor PSF type for isolation, eROSITA-DE only for l > 180 (must check coverage)

Controls: the known eclipsing WDMS from Parsons+2015 / ZTF-2023 / Gaia-WDMS-2025 that fall inside DES (Stripe 82 and the dec -30 strip) must be recovered by the pair test on NSC's own configuration before any yield claim (lesson 10)
selection: Footprint: DES wide 5,000 deg^2 (|b| > 20). Pool: nsc_dr2.object with class_star > 0.8, rmag 20-21.5 (bright enough that a 2.5-mag eclipse stays above depth95 with margin), ndetr >= 6, ndet >= 25 => ~6-10 million objects; pre-filter: any of rrms/grms/irms/zrms > 0.3 mag (a single 1.5-mag drop among 10 points gives rms ~ 0.47; typical rrms at r = 21 is 0.03-0.05, measured mean 0.047) => ~2% => 150-250k objects; pull all their meas rows (~1e7 rows, ~1,000 batched TAP queries by objectid). Event definition: two exposures at the same pointing with |dt| <= 3 min (the 2.0-min pairs) in which BOTH measurements are >= 1.2 mag below the object's own per-band median, in mag_auto AND mag_aper2, flags = 0, x and y > 50 px from the CCD edge, exposure fwhm < 1.6 arcsec and zptermsig nominal, per-row centroid within 0.2 arcsec of the object position; neighbour control: >= 90% of stars of similar magnitude within 3 arcmin on the same CCD are within 0.1 mag of their medians in both exposures. Amplitude threshold 1.2 mag excludes RR Lyrae (r amplitude <= 0.9), delta Scuti and contact binaries; ordinary Algols with 1.2-2 mag total eclipses remain as the bulk bycatch (~5-10x the WD systems) and go to VSX as EA. WD-binary tagging: blue g-r (< 0.6) with red r-z or a VHS J excess, GALEX NUV detection, or Gaia BP-RP + parallax placing it between the WD and MS sequences. Expected funnel: 6-10 M -> 150-250k -> ~2,000 single-exposure drops -> ~300-1,500 pair-corroborated deep-eclipse events -> 20-90 WD-binary-coloured candidates.
main_false_positive_channel: Instrumental faint-flux artefacts in ONE exposure: partial masking (cosmic-ray/bad-column masks inside the Kron aperture), CCD edges and chip gaps, tracking/seeing outliers, and Kron-aperture deblending failures near neighbours (33% of a control star's rows carry flags = 2). These are single-exposure and single-band; the requirement that both members of a 2-minute pair drop by >= 1.2 mag, in both aperture and Kron photometry, with flags = 0, off-edge, and with same-CCD neighbours steady, is the kill (independent artefacts at ~1e-4 per exposure square to ~1e-8 per pair). Astrophysical FPs: deep-eclipsing Algol-type MS binaries (real, boring, ~10x more numerous; separated only by colour/SED, so the WD label is candidate-grade), and rare high-PM stars whose measurement falls outside NSC's match radius (produces missing rows, not faint rows, so it does not enter).
credit_channel: VSX (named credit) as EA/EA: with two in-eclipse points plus the composite-SED argument; a candidate list for the eclipsing-WDMS community (Parsons/Sheffield, Rebassa-Mansergas/UPC, van Roestel, SAAO/ULTRACAM-NTT users) who need period and radial-velocity follow-up - the community-confirm mode. A co-authored catalogue paper only if >= 20 candidates survive refereeing.
why_not_already_done: The natural owners and why they did not: (a) ZTF WD groups (Burdge, van Roestel, Kupfer, Brown) are limited to dec > -31 and r < 20.5; the 2025 Gaia DR3 WDMS catalogue states that only 920 of its 1,312 systems are even accessible to ZTF and finds its 67 eclipsers exclusively with ZTF/CRTS light curves - the far south at r > 20 is a documented hole. (b) Parsons/Rebassa-Mansergas used SDSS+CRTS (north, r < 20). (c) Kilic's DECam minute-cadence survey found 1 eclipsing WD+dM in one 3 deg^2 pointing over 8 half-nights - correct physics, 1/1,700 of the area. (d) The DES collaboration's stellar variability work (Stringer RR Lyrae; Cerny/Drlica-Wagner dwarf galaxies) modelled periodic RR Lyrae on sparse multi-band data and never built a single-visit eclipse test; DES has no per-exposure public light-curve product of its own - NSC DR2 is the only one, and NSC's variability flags (rms/MAD-based, nsigvar) were released as a 10-sigma catalogue of periodic variables, not searched for 2-of-45 events. (e) Rubin will do this trivially from 2027 (negative-flux DIA sources in the alert stream) - which is precisely why nobody at the professional level is investing in it now, and why the lane has an 18-month clock.
session_lesson_exploited: Lesson 4 (per-epoch centroid + per-frame depth is the honest reference): use per-row ra/dec and per-exposure depth95 so an eclipse is a measured faint point with a coincident centroid, not a threshold artefact. Lesson 10 (recover your own template on the pipeline's configuration): known eclipsing WDMS in Stripe 82/dec -30 strip are the templates. Lesson 6 (nsc_dr2.meas dated rows) and the verified 2.0-min pair structure turn a sparse 10-epoch survey into a self-corroborating one. Lesson 5 (VHS/UKIDSS barely used): VHS J is the M-dwarf detector. Lesson 9 (prove coverage): GALEX/eROSITA/VHS tile coverage per object before citing a null. Lesson 7-analogue: batch NSC pulls by objectid and expect empty-200 style failures - checkpoint and re-verify counts.
feasibility_notes: Access: anonymous Data Lab TAP works (verified today on object/exposure/meas); the object-table pre-filter over 5,000 deg^2 needs ~50-100 regional queries, the meas pull ~1,000 batched queries (~1e7 rows, ~2-4 GB CSV); anonymous rate/row limits unmeasured - pilot on 50 deg^2 first. Compute: laptop or the NUC; all-sky SQLite/parquet of pre-filtered objects ~1-2 GB. Archive-only confirmation: PARTIAL - the eclipse event itself is archive-confirmed (two independent exposures), the WD nature is SED-level, and the period is NOT obtainable (2-6 in-eclipse points over 6 yr alias hopelessly), so every object is a candidate for the community to time. Labor: ~2 weeks to a refereed candidate list. Kill rule: bottleneck is vetting labor (colour/SED arguments per object), not telescope time, as long as the deliverable is a candidate list. Clock: Rubin negative-DIA discoveries in bulk by ~2027-28.
novelty_per_labor_guess: MEDIUM-HIGH: 20-90 candidate eclipsing WD binaries (plus 0-3 potentially rarer double-WD/WD+BD eclipsers and hundreds of routine deep Algols) for ~2 weeks, in a hemisphere and magnitude range with zero prior time-domain coverage; per-object novelty is high but confirmation-grade is candidate-only, which caps the credit at VSX EA: entries plus a community hand-off.
