title: Deep-vs-deep state-change ledger in the DES-SN + HELM fields: sources at r = 20-22.5 that switch state for >= 10 days or permanently across 2013-2022, using expected-coverage ledgers (NSC chip footprints, HELM epoch lists) so that censored non-detections count as faint-state measurements
what_we_would_find: Long-duration low/high state transitions in faint Galactic point sources: magnetic CVs (polars) and novalikes at 2-6 kpc switching between high and low accretion states (2-4 mag, weeks-years), dust-occultation dips and long-period total eclipses (>= 10 d) in stars that no shallow survey has ever seen in the faint state, and permanent transitions in either direction (a source present at r ~ 21-22 in 2013-2016 and gone to < 23.5 in every later epoch, or the reverse) - the deep-vs-deep, same-instrument version of the closed turn-on lane. Expected counts, honestly small: the CV column gives 5-16 CVs in 27 deg^2; polars+novalikes ~30% => 2-5; state changes within 9 yr in 60-80% => 1-4 state-switching magnetic CV/novalike candidates; 0-2 dust-dip/long-eclipse oddities; the density scaling from the closed ZTF-depth state-cycler search (< 0.01 per deg^2 at r <= 20.5) times the 10-30x volume gain to r <= 22.5 gives 0.1-0.3 per deg^2 => 3-8 objects in 27 deg^2, consistent. AGN state changes will be the numerous bycatch (hundreds; HELM's own turf; excluded by extendedness + WISE + zero PM).
data_sources: nsc_dr2.chip (vertex_ra1-4 / vertex_dec1-4 per CCD, 24.4M rows) to build the expected-coverage ledger: for each object, every DECam CCD footprint 2012-2019 that contains it, with that chip's depth95/depth10sig, fwhm, zptermsig; nsc_dr2.meas rows for the object give the realised detections; the difference is the censored set

HELM DR1 light curves per field (2019A-2022A; no forced photometry, so missing rows are censoring by construction) plus HELM's per-field exposure lists to define expected epochs; NSC covers HELM's first 9 months (Feb-Nov 2019) as an overlap for cross-calibrating PSF vs Kron magnitudes

DES-SN5YR DiffImg light curves for the positive direction 2013-2018 (a turn-on that stays on IS detected by DiffImg as a long-lived positive residual and survives in the 31,636 set; a turn-off is not, since DiffImg only examines positive detections - hence the NSC ledger is the only route for fading)

Object pool verified today: 2,008 point sources per deg^2 at r 20-22.5 with >= 50 r detections in the C3 box (mean ndetr = 589) => ~54,000 objects over the 10 DES-SN pointings; comparison-star control uses same-CCD stars within 3 arcmin

LS DR10 forced unWISE (AGN kill), Gaia DR3 PM, VHS J/Ks (the donor/companion in the low state), eROSITA-DE where l > 180 (E1/E2, S-CVZ: check), Chandra CDF-S/XMM-LSS deep X-ray catalogues for C3/X3 (a polar in low state is still an X-ray source)
selection: Fields: the 10 DES-SN pointings (27 deg^2), 2013-2019 via NSC and 2019-2022 via HELM; HELM's COSMOS/S-CVZ (11 deg^2) for 2019-22 only. Pool: point sources (class_star > 0.8) with median r = 20-22.5 and >= 50 r detections (~54,000 objects). Ledger: for each object list all covering exposures (chip vertices) with depth95 >= object median + 1.5 mag in that band; realised rows come from meas. Event types: (A) 'low-state run' = >= 3 consecutive expected epochs (>= 10 d, >= 20 expected exposures across bands) in which the object is either missing or measured >= 1.5 mag below median, while >= 90% of same-CCD comparison stars of similar magnitude are detected within 0.1 mag of their medians, followed by recovery; (B) 'permanent transition' = a single change-point splitting the 2013-2022 baseline into two states differing by >= 1.5 mag with each state holding for >= 1 season, with the same comparison-star control; (C) the HELM-catalogue-seeding caveat means turn-ons after 2019 are only visible via NSC for 2019 and DiffImg before it, so direction B is asymmetric - state it. Then: WISE/PM/extendedness AGN kill, X-ray counterpart check for polar candidates, and per-object same-night reproduction of every state boundary (>= 2 exposures). Injection test: insert synthetic 10-d gaps and 1.5-mag steps into 1,000 control light curves and require >= 90% recovery at < 1% false-run rate before reading real candidates.
main_false_positive_channel: Coverage bookkeeping errors masquerading as faint states: an object near a CCD edge/gap or under a bright-star mask that is 'expected' by the vertex ledger but never measurable; PSF-dependent Kron losses in bad-seeing runs (a whole visit fainter by 0.3-0.5 mag); HELM-vs-NSC magnitude-system offsets (PSF vs AUTO, DES-DR2-tied vs Gaia/PS1-tied zero points) producing a fake 2019 step; high-proper-motion objects drifting out of the match radius over 9 yr (>= 150 mas/yr moves >= 1.3 arcsec); AGN on unresolved hosts (numerous, killed by WISE/PM/morphology). The comparison-star control on the same CCD in the same exposures is the primary kill for the first three; the injection test is the gate.
credit_channel: VSX (named credit) for state-switching CVs (AM:/NL: with the high/low light curves), AstroNote/TNS only for a genuinely unexplained permanent disappearance after all artefact channels are closed; anything AGN-like is handed to HELM's authors rather than filed.
why_not_already_done: HELM (Shen/Zhang) will harvest AGN state changes in exactly these fields and will not look at Galactic point sources; DES-SN's DiffImg by design never examined negative residuals, so fading events were structurally invisible to the collaboration; the DDF team's Galactic-variable work is in their two Galactic fields, not here; polar/novalike state-change searches (ZTF, ASAS-SN, Catalina) stop at r ~ 20.5 and cannot see the low state at all for anything beyond ~1 kpc; NSC's own variability flags (MAD/rms/nsigvar) are single-number statistics that a decade-long two-state light curve moves only modestly and that cannot represent censoring. The honest reason it is not done is also that the yield is small (1-4 objects) and the ledger work is real - which is why this is a by-product lane to run on the same NSC/HELM pulls as Lane 1, not a stand-alone programme.
session_lesson_exploited: Lessons 1 and 2 directly: HELM's catalogue is seeded from the DES-DR2 coadd and has no forced photometry, so non-detections are informative faint-state measurements only when the expected-coverage ledger exists - the ledger IS the lane. Lesson 3 (constant-bright new sources are invisible to brokers) is why permanent transitions need a per-exposure ledger rather than DIA. What changed versus the closed turn-on and bimodal state-cycler lanes: same instrument, same depth on both sides (DECam vs DECam, no blend/threshold pathology from comparing a deep sharp survey to a shallow coarse one), per-exposure rather than object-average statistics, same-CCD comparison stars, both signs of change, and 10-30x the search volume of the ZTF-depth cycler search. Lesson 10 (injection-tested recovery before absence claims) is mandatory here because five silent pipeline bugs were caught only by controls this session.
feasibility_notes: Access: same anonymous Data Lab TAP as Lanes 1-2 (verified) plus HELM's open directories; the ledger needs the chip table restricted to the 10 pointings (~50k CCD footprints) and ~54,000 objects x ~2,500 covering exposures = ~1.3e8 expected entries and a similar number of meas rows (~1,400 batched queries, several hours to a day of automated pulling, ~10 GB local parquet; fits on the NUC). Compute: modest. Archive-only confirmation: YES for the state change itself (two states, each reproduced in many exposures) - the physical class (polar vs novalike vs dust) stays candidate-grade without spectra. Labor: 2-3 weeks including the injection harness; run it only as an add-on once Lane 1's NSC/HELM pulls exist. Rubin DP1/DP2 cannot be used (data-rights-only). Kill rule: bottleneck is vetting/ledger labor, not telescope time.
novelty_per_labor_guess: LOW-MEDIUM: 1-4 new state-switching faint CVs plus 0-2 oddities for 2-3 weeks of heavy bookkeeping; the phenomenon class (faint-state to faint-state transitions at r 22-24) is genuinely unobservable by any other survey, which is the only reason to keep it on the menu, and only as a by-product of Lane 1's data pulls.
